元日にも春節（旧正月）にも使える新年のあいさつ。中国では春節のほうが盛大に祝いま: A New Year greeting you can use both on January 1 and at Spring Festival (Chinese New Year), though in China Spring Festival is celebrated on a much bigger scale. You can simply reply with 「新年快乐！」 too.
あけましておめでとう！今年もみんなよろしくね！: Happy New Year! I hope everyone will keep looking out for me this year too!
年の初めに「心機一転がんばろう」という気持ちを表す決まり文句。部屋を片づけた時や: A set phrase for the "turn over a new leaf" feeling at the start of the year, often heard in company New Year greetings. You can also use it jokingly after tidying your room or getting a haircut.
髪型変えたんだ、新しい年だから心機一転！: I got a new haircut, new year, fresh start!
千里の道も一歩から: A journey of a thousand miles begins with a single step
大きな目標も足元の一歩から始まるという意味。『老子』の言葉で、日本語のことわざと: Even a big goal starts with one step from where you stand. It comes from the Laozi (and is the source of the English saying), and it's a perfect encouragement for someone starting something new.
難しく考えないで。千里の道も一歩から、まずは毎日単語10個から始めよう。: Don't worry about how hard it is, a journey of a thousand miles begins with a single step. Start with ten words a day.
目標を宣言する（フラグを立てる）: to publicly declare a goal ("raise a flag")
新年の抱負など、目標を宣言すること。日本のネット用語「フラグ」と違い、目標を公言: Declaring a goal, such as a New Year's resolution. It has nothing to do with a warning sign; the core meaning is announcing your goal to everyone, though it's often used with a self-deprecating punchline about a "flag" you won't be able to keep.
まず宣言しとく：今年こそ5キロやせる！: Let me raise a flag first: this year I'm definitely losing ten jin (5 kg)!
しばらく会っていなかった相手に。友達にも目上にも使える万能フレーズ。返しも「好久: For someone you haven't seen in a while, and it works with friends and superiors alike. You can reply with 「好久不见！」 too; it's said to be the origin of the English "long time no see."
お久しぶり！全然変わってないね！: Long time no see! You haven't changed a bit!
契約や協力が決まったとき、握手しながら言う定番の一言。「楽しく協力しましょう」が: The standard line said with a handshake once a contract or partnership is agreed. Literally "let's cooperate happily," it's like saying "I look forward to working with you" in English.
契約が無事にまとまりました。今後ともよろしくお願いします！: The contract's signed. Here's to a great partnership!
新しいことを始めるときは最初が一番大変だ、という意味のことわざ。始めたばかりで苦: A saying meaning the start is always the hardest part of anything new. Saying 「万事开头难，慢慢来」 to someone who's just started and is struggling is a gentle encouragement.
発音は最初は難しくて当然、何事も最初が大変だからね。: Pronunciation is bound to be hard when you first start learning. Every beginning is hard, after all.
「〜死了」は「死ぬほど〜」という強調で、本当に死ぬわけではありません。「热死了」: 「〜死了」 means "to death," an intensifier that doesn't mean anyone is literally dying; you can attach it to almost anything, as in 「热死了」 「累死了」 「饿死了」. In the north, indoor heating in winter is so warm that the contrast with outside is a shock.
今日はマイナス10度、寒すぎる！: It's minus ten degrees today. It's freezing!
辛さ控えめでお願いします: Go easy on the chili, please.
四川料理や湖南料理の店で役立つ一言。「中辣」でも日本人にはかなり辛いことが多いの: A handy line in Sichuan or Hunan restaurants. Even 「中辣」 (medium) is often very hot for many foreign visitors, so be careful; if you want no heat at all ask for 「不要辣」, or 「微辣」 for just a little.
すみません、この料理は辛さ控えめで。辛いのがあまり得意じゃなくて。: Excuse me, could you go easy on the chili in this dish? I can't really handle spicy food.
友情に厚い行動をしてくれた友達へのほめ言葉。「義理堅い」「頼りになる」の意味。逆: Praise for a friend who has done something loyal and generous for you, meaning "loyal" or "reliable." The opposite, 「不够意思」, means "that's not very friendly of you" or "cold."
わざわざ空港まで迎えに来てくれるなんて、ほんと友達思いだね！: You came all the way to the airport to pick me up? You're a true friend!
ボーナス出た？: Did you get your year-end bonus?
「年终奖」は年末から春節前に出る年末ボーナス。同僚や友達同士でよく話題になります: 「年终奖」 is the year-end bonus paid between the end of the year and Spring Festival. It's a common topic among coworkers and friends, but asking the amount directly can be rude, so a light 「发了吗？」 is the safe way to ask.
ボーナス出た？うちの部署は来週らしいよ。: Did you get your year-end bonus? I heard our department gets it next week.
「溜（liù）」と同じ発音で、「上手い・すごい」の意味。ゲーム配信のコメントで生: It sounds the same as 「溜（liù）」, meaning "skilled, awesome." It started in comments on game livestreams and is now used in everyday chat, much like typing "insane!" or "so good lol" in English.
1分でパソコン直したの？すごっ！: You fixed the computer in one minute? Awesome!
雪が降り始めたときの一言。「了」は状況の変化を表し、「降ってきた！」という発見の: What you say when snow starts falling; 「了」 marks a change of situation, giving it a "hey, it's started snowing!" feeling of discovery. People in the north routinely post photos of the first snow on social media, and for people in the south snow is especially exciting news.
窓の外見て、雪が降ってきたよ！: Look out the window, it's snowing outside!
旅行で必ず役立つ一言。「厕所」も通じますが、「洗手间」のほうが上品です。お店では: A line you'll definitely need when traveling. 「厕所」 is also understood, but 「洗手间」 is more polite, and in shops you'll often see signs saying 「卫生间」.
すみません、トイレはどこですか？2階ですか？: Excuse me, where's the restroom? Is it on the second floor?
うれしい知らせを聞いたとき、ほっとしたときに。「太〜了」は「すごく〜」の基本パタ: For when you hear good news or feel relieved. 「太〜了」 is the basic "so ..." pattern, and you can extend it to 「太棒了」 「太可惜了」 and so on.
試験受かったの？よかったね、おめでとう！: You passed the exam? That's great, congratulations!
料理が出てきたときに、相手に早く食べるよう勧める一言。中国では温かい料理を大事に: Said when food arrives, urging others to start eating right away. Hot food matters a lot in China, so you'll hear this again and again at the table; when someone says it to you, don't be too reserved, say 「好，我不客气了」 and dig in.
餃子ゆでたてだよ、熱いうちに食べて！: The dumplings just came out of the pot, eat them while they're hot!
チケット取れた？: Did you manage to get tickets?
春節前の帰省ラッシュ「春运」の時期の定番の質問。発売と同時に列車の切符を「奪い合: The standard question during 「春运」, the Spring Festival travel rush. Train tickets are "fought over" the moment they go on sale, hence 「抢」; if you got one say 「抢到了！」, and if not, something like 「没抢到，只能站票了」.
帰省の切符取れた？私は立ち席しか取れなかったよ。: Did you get a ticket home? I could only get a standing ticket.
温故知新: Review the old to learn the new
古いことを学び直して新しい知識を得ること。『論語』の言葉で、日本語と全く同じ四字: Gaining new knowledge by going back over what you've learned. A four-character idiom from the Analects, it's used in Chinese when talking about the importance of studying and reviewing.
試験前に復習して、間違えた問題をもう一度解こう。: Review before the exam: go over the questions you got wrong once more.
臘八が過ぎればもう正月: Once Laba has passed, New Year is here
旧暦12月8日の「腊八」に、雑穀のおかゆ「腊八粥」を食べる習慣があり、この日から: On 「腊八」, the 8th day of the 12th lunar month, people eat 「腊八粥」, a porridge of mixed grains, and preparations for Spring Festival are said to begin that day. The saying captures the end-of-year mood and is good for year-end small talk.
今日は臘八粥を飲んだよ。これからもうお正月ムードだね。: I had Laba porridge today. Once Laba has passed, New Year is practically here!
よろしくお願いします: Nice to meet you. / I look forward to working with you.
初対面や新しい職場でのあいさつ。日本語の「よろしく」ほど毎回は使わず、自己紹介の: A greeting for first meetings or a new workplace. It isn't something you say every time; it suits formal moments like the end of a self-introduction, and friends don't need to say it at all.
田中と申します。入社したばかりです、よろしくお願いします。: My name is Tanaka. I've just joined the company, and I look forward to working with you.
やることがなくて暇なときのぼやき。「无聊」は「退屈・つまらない」の意味で、人や話: A grumble when you have nothing to do. 「无聊」 means "bored, boring," and said of a person or a conversation it becomes a criticism, "pointless, silly." It's often heard on the last day of a long weekend or while waiting around.
雨で出かけられなくて、家で退屈すぎる。: It's raining so I can't go out. I'm bored to death at home.
もとは出勤のタイムカード。今は人気スポットや店に行って写真を投稿することや、勉強: Originally it meant punching a time card at work. Now it's used for visiting a popular spot or shop and posting photos, and also for logging that you kept up a study or exercise habit; 「网红打卡地」 means an Instagrammable spot.
今日は中国語を30分勉強した、記録っと！: Studied Chinese for 30 minutes today. Checked in!
お正月は実家に帰るの？: Are you going home for New Year?
春節が近づくと同僚や友達とかならず交わす会話。中国では春節に故郷へ帰り家族と過ご: A conversation you're bound to have with coworkers and friends as Spring Festival approaches, since going back to your hometown to spend it with family is the most important custom in China. Natural answers are 「回，后天走」 or 「今年不回了」.
お正月は実家に帰るの？私は来週の金曜に帰るよ。: Are you going home for New Year? I'm leaving next Friday.
ネットショッピングで最もよく聞く質問の一つ。「包邮」は「送料込み」のこと。店員と: One of the most common questions in online shopping; 「包邮」 means "shipping included." Many people check this first in the chat with the seller.
すみません、この服は送料無料ですか？: Hi dear, does this top come with free shipping?
いつもの場所でね！: See you at the usual place!
友達同士で待ち合わせ場所を言うとき、「いつもの店・場所」を指す一言。言わなくても: What friends say when arranging to meet at "the usual place or restaurant." It shows a closeness where nothing more needs to be said, just like "see you at the usual spot" in English.
今夜7時、いつものとこで会おう！: Tonight at seven, see you at the usual place!
お正月の買い物はすんだ？: Have you done your New Year shopping?
「年货」は春節用の食べ物や飾りなどの買い物のこと。春節前はスーパーや市場が「年货: 「年货」 means the food, decorations and other things bought for Spring Festival. Before the holiday, supermarkets and markets are packed with people buying 「年货」, and more and more people buy it all online; 「办年货」 means "to do the New Year shopping."
正月の買い物はすんだ？私は春聯だけまだなんだ。: Have you finished your New Year shopping? All I still need are the couplets.
寝る前のあいさつ。チャットの最後に送ることも多いです。親しい間柄では「晚安，好梦: A goodnight greeting, often sent at the end of a chat. With people you're close to, adding 「晚安，好梦！」 ("Good night, sweet dreams!") comes across as warm.
先に寝るね。おやすみ、また明日！: I'm going to bed. Good night, see you tomorrow!
空いている部屋はありますか？: Do you have any rooms available?
予約なしでホテルや宿に入ったときの基本フレーズ。「今晚还有空房吗？」と日付を入れ: The basic phrase when you walk into a hotel or guesthouse without a reservation; adding the date, as in 「今晚还有空房吗？」, makes it clearer. During holidays places are often 「客满」 (fully booked), so booking early is the safe choice.
こんにちは、今夜空いている部屋はありますか？2人です。: Hello, do you still have a room available tonight? For two.
実家で大晦日のごちそうを食べる: to go home for the New Year's Eve dinner
「年夜饭」は大晦日の夜に家族そろって食べるごちそう。一年で一番大事な食事で、遠く: 「年夜饭」 is the feast the whole family eats together on New Year's Eve. It's the most important meal of the year, and many people want to come home for it even if they live far away; more and more families now book it at a restaurant.
どんなに忙しくても、大晦日は家に帰って年越しのごちそうを食べなきゃ。: No matter how busy I am, I have to go home for the New Year's Eve dinner.
春節の時期に会った人への口頭のあいさつ。北方でよく使われ、親しみのある響きです。: A spoken greeting for people you meet around Spring Festival. It's common in the north and sounds warm and friendly, and you can use it with anyone in the days before and after the holiday.
王さん、新年おめでとうございます！果物を持ってきました。: Happy New Year, Auntie Wang! I brought you some fruit.
旧正月を祝う最も一般的なあいさつ。メッセージやカードにも使えます。「新年快乐」と: The most common greeting for Lunar New Year, also fine for messages and cards. It's almost the same as 「新年快乐」 but makes it clear you mean Spring Festival; reply with 「春节快乐！」 or 「你也是！」.
ご家族とともに、よい春節を。健康でありますように！: Wishing you and your family a happy Spring Festival and good health!
新年のごあいさつに参りました: Happy New Year to you! (a New Year visit)
春節に親戚や目上の人へ新年のあいさつをする時の決まり文句。「拜年」は年始回りのこ: The set phrase for paying New Year respects to relatives and elders at Spring Festival; 「拜年」 means making New Year visits. Many people now do their 「拜年」 by video call or message, and saying it might even earn you a red envelope!
おじいちゃんおばあちゃん、新年おめでとう！長生きしてね！: Grandpa, Grandma, Happy New Year! Wishing you good health and a long life!
春節の定番のお祝いの言葉。商売繁盛や財運を願います。子どもが「恭喜发财，红包拿来: The classic Spring Festival blessing, wishing for good business and wealth. It's a running joke for kids to add 「恭喜发财，红包拿来！」 ("now hand over the red envelope!").
お金持ちになりますように！今年も商売繁盛でありますように！: May you prosper! I hope your business does better and better this year!
グループチャットで配られる電子お年玉「红包」を、早い者勝ちで受け取ること。金額は: Grabbing a digital red envelope 「红包」 handed out in a group chat, first come, first served. The amounts are random, family and friend groups go wild over it at Spring Festival, and even a small amount gets celebrated as 「手气好」 (lucky).
グループで誰かがお年玉配ってて、5元ゲットした！: Someone in the group sent red envelopes, and I grabbed five yuan!
毎年ゆとりがありますように: May you have surplus every year!
「余（余り）」と「鱼（魚）」が同じ発音なので、春節の食卓には魚料理が欠かせません: Because 「余」 (surplus) sounds the same as 「鱼」 (fish), fish is a must on the Spring Festival table. Leaving some of the fish uneaten instead of finishing it is also done for good luck.
大晦日の魚は少し残しておこう、毎年ゆとりがあるようにね。: Let's leave a bit of the New Year's Eve fish, for surplus every year.
すべてが思いどおりにいきますように: May everything go as you wish!
春節やお祝いの席での定番の祝福の言葉。「身体健康，万事如意！」と組み合わせるとあ: A standard blessing at Spring Festival and other celebrations; pairing it as 「身体健康，万事如意！」 makes it sound like a proper greeting. It works in New Year cards and messages and is safe to use with superiors.
新しい一年、ご健康とご多幸をお祈りします！: Wishing you good health and that everything goes your way in the new year!
驚きや感動を表す感嘆詞。きれいな景色、豪華な料理、意外な話などに。若者っぽいカジ: An exclamation of surprise or delight, for beautiful scenery, a lavish meal or a surprising story. It sounds young and casual, close to "Whoa!" or "No way, that's amazing!" in English.
うわぁ、この花火きれいすぎ！: Wow, these fireworks are way too beautiful!
願いがかないますように！: May all your wishes come true!
「心で思ったことが実現する」という祝福。新年や誕生日のメッセージによく使われ、友: A blessing meaning "may what you wish for in your heart come true." It's common in New Year and birthday messages, works with friends and superiors alike, and is a perfect encouragement for someone taking exams or job hunting.
あけましておめでとう！願いがかないますように！: Happy New Year! May all your wishes come true!
旅行や遊びに出かける人への見送りの言葉。英語のHave fun!にあたります。返: A send-off for someone going on a trip or an outing, the equivalent of the English "Have fun!" A natural reply is something like 「谢谢！给你带礼物」 ("I'll bring you a souvenir").
明日から海南島に行くの？いいなあ、楽しんできてね！: You're off to Hainan tomorrow? I'm so jealous. Have fun!
お正月らしさが年々薄れてきたね: New Year feels less and less festive.
「年味儿」は春節らしい雰囲気のこと。昔に比べて行事が簡素になったと感じる人がよく: 「年味儿」 means the festive Spring Festival atmosphere. People who feel the celebrations have become simpler than in the past often say this, in nostalgic small talk usually followed by 「小时候的年才有意思」.
最近はみんなスマホばかり見てて、お正月らしさがなくなってきたね。: Now everyone's just looking at their phones. New Year feels less and less festive.
ちょっと安くしてよ: Can you make it a bit cheaper?
値切るときの定番。「能便宜点吗？」と疑問形にするとやわらかく聞こえます。市場や個: The standard haggling line; making it a question, 「能便宜点吗？」, sounds softer. At markets and small shops, just asking can get you a little off.
店長さん、2つ買うから少し安くしてよ。: Boss, I'm buying two, can you make it a bit cheaper?
仕事始め、おめでとう！: Here's to a great start back at work!
春節明けの仕事始めの日に交わすあいさつ。職場では上司が社員に「开工红包」を配る習: A greeting exchanged on the first working day after Spring Festival. At some companies the boss hands out a 「开工红包」 (back-to-work red envelope) to staff, and sending coworkers 「新年开工大吉！」 is a standard message.
皆さん、仕事始めおめでとう。今年も一緒にがんばろう！: Everyone, here's to a great start back at work. Let's give it our all together again this year!
友達が何かを成し遂げたときのほめ言葉。言い方によっては「よくやるよ」と呆れるニュ: Praise for a friend who has pulled something off. Depending on tone it can mean "you're unbelievable" in an exasperated way, so say it clearly with a smile.
一人でこんなにたくさん料理作ったの？やるじゃん！: You made this whole table of food by yourself? You're amazing!
突然声をかけられたり、驚かされたりしたときに。「一跳」は「一回飛び上がる」で、跳: For when someone suddenly speaks to you or startles you. 「一跳」 means "one jump," jumping out of your skin in surprise, and it's a very common everyday expression.
なんで急に後ろにいるの？びっくりした！: Why are you suddenly behind me? You scared me!
中国のバレンタインは男性から女性に花やプレゼントを贈るのが一般的で、日本の「女性: In China, Valentine's Day usually means men giving women flowers or gifts, and there's almost no custom of obligatory chocolate for coworkers. Qixi is also called "Chinese Valentine's Day."
ハッピーバレンタイン！この花束、あなたに。: Happy Valentine's Day, darling! These flowers are for you.
一目見て恋に落ちること。人だけでなく、物や場所にも使えます。「我对这件衣服一见钟: Falling in love at first glance, and it can be used for things and places as well as people. It comes up often in conversation, as in 「我对这件衣服一见钟情」 ("I fell in love with this top at first sight").
お店でこのカップに一目惚れして、すぐ買っちゃった。: I saw this mug in the shop, fell in love with it at first sight and bought it right away.
「絶対やらない」と言っていた人が、結局それを気に入ってしまう様子を笑うネット語。: Internet slang that laughs at someone who swore they'd never do something and ends up loving it, and it isn't limited to food. Used about yourself, it's a self-deprecating punchline: "I take it back, I'm hooked."
夜食は食べないって言ったのに、一口食べたら最高すぎた！: I said I wouldn't eat a late-night snack, but after one bite... so good!
メニューが読めない時や迷った時の救世主。「招牌菜（看板料理）是什么？」と聞くのも: A lifesaver when you can't read the menu or can't decide; asking 「招牌菜（看板料理）是什么？」 ("what's your signature dish?") is also a good idea. It can lead you to local flavors when traveling.
初めて来たんですが、おすすめはありますか？: It's my first time here. Do you have any recommendations?
休みをいただきたいのですが: I'd like to take some time off.
上司に休暇を申し出るときの基本フレーズ。「请假」は「休みをとる」こと。「请一天假: The basic phrase for asking your boss for leave; 「请假」 means "to take time off." You can add the number of days, as in 「请一天假」, or give a reason such as 「病假」 (sick leave) or 「事假」 (personal leave).
部長、明日休みをいただきたいのですが。病院に行こうと思いまして。: Manager, I'd like to take tomorrow off to go to the hospital.
旅行仲間との予定確認に。答えは「八点出发」のように。集合場所も聞くなら「在哪儿集: For checking plans with travel companions; answer with something like 「八点出发」. To ask where to meet, say 「在哪儿集合？」, and since you'll hear these often on tours, learn to catch them.
明日何時に出発する？ホテルの入り口に集合？: What time are we leaving tomorrow? Are we meeting at the hotel entrance?
一度言ったことは変えない、という約束の確認。友達と予定を決めた時に「那就一言为定: Confirming a promise you won't go back on; when making plans with a friend, you seal it with 「那就一言为定！」. It's close to English "It's a deal!" or "You have my word," and as casual as a pinky promise.
来週の土曜に一緒に山登りね、約束だよ！: Hiking together next Saturday, it's a deal!
お返事お待ちしております: I look forward to your reply.
ビジネスメールの締めの定番。「您」で丁寧さを出しています。日本語の「ご返信お待ち: A standard closing line for business emails, with 「您」 adding politeness. It works just like "I look forward to hearing from you" in English.
資料をお送りしました。お返事お待ちしております。: I've sent the materials. I look forward to your reply.

6月上旬の全国統一大学入試「高考」を受ける受験生への応援の言葉。社会全体で注目さ: Encouragement for students taking 「高考」, the national college entrance exam in early June. It's a huge event the whole country pays attention to, with people even keeping quiet around exam sites, and you can say it to the students' families too.
明日はいよいよ本番、入試がんばって、きっと大丈夫！: The exam is tomorrow. Good luck on the gaokao, you've got this!
中国語には「いただきます」にあたる決まった言葉がなく、こうした一言で食べ始めます: Chinese has no fixed phrase like a pre-meal grace or "bon appétit," so people start eating with a casual line like this. When elders are at the table, it's good manners to wait for them to pick up their chopsticks first.
料理が全部そろったよ、さあ食べよう！: All the dishes are here. Let's dig in, everyone!
端午節に食べる「粽子」は、北方では甘いもの、南方では肉入りのしょっぱいものが多く: The 「粽子」 eaten at the Dragon Boat Festival are mostly sweet in the north and savory with meat in the south, and which one people prefer is debated online every year. As a foreigner, answering "I like both" keeps the peace.
もうすぐ端午節だね、甘いちまきとしょっぱいちまき、どっちが好き？: The Dragon Boat Festival is almost here. Do you prefer sweet or savory zongzi?
相手を楽しませたり、安心させたりする心の面での価値のこと。「他很会提供情绪价值（: The emotional value of making someone feel happy or reassured, used as in 「他很会提供情绪价值」 ("he's great at making people feel good"). It's a new term often heard in talk about relationships and friendships.
彼女と話すとすごく楽しい、気分を最高に上げてくれる。: Talking with her is so much fun. She maxes out the emotional value.
端午節、健やかに: Wishing you good health this Dragon Boat Festival!
旧暦5月5日の端午節のあいさつ。もとは厄除けの行事なので「快乐」より「安康」がふ: A greeting for the Dragon Boat Festival on the 5th day of the 5th lunar month, the day people eat zongzi. Since it was originally about warding off evil, some say 「安康」 is more fitting than 「快乐」, but 「端午节快乐」 is also widely used.
端午節、健やかにね！ちまき食べるの忘れずに。: Wishing you good health this Dragon Boat Festival! Don't forget to eat zongzi.
服屋で試着したい時の一言。「试衣间」は試着室。店によっては試着できる枚数が決まっ: For trying on clothes in a shop; 「试衣间」 is the fitting room. Some shops limit how many items you can take in or give you a numbered tag, so learn it together with 「可以试一下吗？」.
すみません、このズボンを試したいのですが、試着室はどこですか？: Hi, I'd like to try on these pants. Where's the fitting room?
友達と出かけた時の定番。「咱们」は話し相手を含む「私たち」で、親しみのある響きで: The classic line when out with friends. 「咱们」 is "we" including the listener and sounds friendly, and the standard thing to say when snapping is 「一、二、三，茄子！」, the Chinese "say cheese."
今日はいい天気だし、一緒に写真撮ろう！: The weather's so nice today, let's take a photo together!
「食後に百歩歩けば九十九まで生きられる」という言い伝えの前半。健康のための散歩を: The first half of the saying "walk a hundred steps after a meal and you'll live to ninety-nine," used to recommend a walk for your health. Many people in China stroll in parks and residential compounds after dinner, so the saying is part of daily life.
食べてすぐ横にならないで、食後は少し歩こうよ。: Don't lie down right after eating. Take a walk after meals, you know.
お客さんや友達を見送るときの定番。「ゆっくり歩いて」が直訳で、日本語の「お気をつ: The standard line for seeing off guests or friends. Literally "walk slowly," it's like "take care" or "get home safely" in English; reply with 「好，再见！」.
お気をつけて、またぜひお店にお越しください！: Take care, and please visit our shop again!
長江下流の地域で、梅の実が黄色くなるころの長雨の時期を指す言葉。日本の梅雨と同じ: The long rainy spell in the lower Yangtze region around when plums turn yellow. Like the rainy season in East Asia generally, it's humid and laundry won't dry; in Shanghai and nearby, people also say 「入梅了」 ("the rainy season has started").
梅雨になると、服をいくら干しても乾かない。: Once the plum rains arrive, clothes never dry no matter how you hang them.
友達との別れ際や知り合ったばかりの人に。日本語と同じく社交辞令の場合もあります。: Said when parting from a friend or to someone you've just met. As with "let's grab lunch sometime" in English, it may just be a polite formula; if you mean it, suggest a specific day, like 「周六怎么样？」.
久しぶりだね、今度ご飯行こうよ！: It's been ages. Let's get a meal together sometime!
618セールで何買いだめした？: What did you stock up on for 618?
6月18日前後の大型ネットセール「618」の時期によく交わされる会話。「囤」は「: A question often exchanged around 「618」, the big online sale around June 18; 「囤」 means "to stock up." It's a shopping event on par with Singles' Day (Double 11), and many people buy household goods in bulk.
618セールで何買いだめした？私はティッシュを一箱どーんと買った。: What did you stock up on for 618? I bought a huge box of tissues.
車が山の前まで来れば必ず道がある、つまり困難も何とか切り抜けられるという意味。日: When the cart reaches the mountain there will always be a road, meaning difficulties can be overcome somehow. It's a positive saying, close to "cross that bridge when you come to it" in English.
あまり心配しないで、なんとかなるさ。: Don't worry too much. Things will work out.
6月の第3日曜日の父の日のあいさつ。母の日ほど盛大ではありませんが、メッセージや: A greeting for Father's Day, the third Sunday in June. It's not as big as Mother's Day, but more and more people send messages or gifts; if you feel shy, showing it through actions, like cooking your dad's favorite dish, is the Chinese way.
お父さん、父の日おめでとう！週末ごちそうするね。: Dad, happy Father's Day! I'll treat you to dinner this weekend.
店員さんに声をかけられたときの一言。「随便看看」も同じ意味です。言えばたいてい放: A line for when a shop assistant approaches you; 「随便看看」 means the same. They'll usually leave you alone after you say it, so it's handy when you want to browse at your own pace.
ありがとう、見てるだけです。必要な時は呼びますね。: Thanks, I'm just looking. I'll call you if I need anything.
すごく面白い時の大げさなリアクション。チャットでは「笑死」だけや「哈哈哈」を並べ: An exaggerated reaction to something hilarious. In chat, people often type just 「笑死」 or a string of 「哈哈哈」; it's like "LOL" or "I'm dead" in English, used casually among friends.
あなたが送ってくれた動画、ウケすぎる！: That video you sent me had me dying of laughter!
個室はありますか？: Do you have a private room?
レストランで個室を希望する時の一言。中国の大きめの店には個室「包间」が多く、会食: For asking for a private room in a restaurant. Larger restaurants in China often have private rooms, 「包间」, used for business dinners and family gatherings; check whether there's a 「最低消费」 (minimum spend).
10人で食事会なんですが、個室はありますか？: There are ten of us for a dinner party. Do you have a private room?
中国の大学の卒業は6月ごろ。卒業式で角帽を投げて写真を撮るのが定番です。「祝你前: Chinese universities hold graduation around June, and tossing mortarboards for a photo is a classic. Adding 「祝你前程似锦」 ("wishing you a bright future") conveys your feelings even better, and graduates say it to each other too.
卒業おめでとう！仕事がうまくいき、輝かしい未来がありますように！: Happy graduation! Wishing you success at work and a bright future!
何かあったら言ってね: Come to me if you need anything.
困った時は頼って、と相手を安心させる一言。友達にも同僚にも使えます。「有事随时找: A reassuring line telling someone to rely on you when in trouble, fine with friends and coworkers alike. Making it 「有事随时找我」 sounds even more supportive, and it's more colloquial and friendly than 「有问题随时联系我」.
来たばかりで慣れないでしょ、何かあったら言ってね。: You're new here and don't know your way around yet. Just come to me if you need anything.
飛行機や列車、レストランで座席を希望する時に。通路側は「靠过道的座位」。高速鉄道: For requesting a seat on a plane or train or in a restaurant; an aisle seat is 「靠过道的座位」. On high-speed trains the window seats are lettered 「A」 and 「F」, so you can also ask by seat letter.
すみません、窓側の席をお願いできますか？: Hi, could I have a window seat?
ぶつかり合ったのがきっかけで、かえって仲良くなること。トラブルから友人になった時: Becoming closer precisely because you clashed at first, said with a laugh when a conflict turned into a friendship. It's a positive saying, close to "a fight can clear the air" in English.
私たちはけんかで知り合ったんだ、まさにけんかするほど仲がいいだね。: We met through an argument. Truly, no discord, no concord.
ご両親によろしく伝えてね: Say hi to your parents for me.
友達の家族へのよろしくを伝える一言。中国では友達の両親を「叔叔阿姨」と呼びます。: A line for sending regards to a friend's family; in China you call a friend's parents 「叔叔阿姨」 ("uncle and auntie"). It works just like "say hi to your folks for me," when parting or to a friend heading home.
実家に帰るなら、ご両親によろしく伝えてね。: If you go back home, say hello to your mom and dad for me.
梅雨から夏にかけての、湿気が多くじめじめした暑さを表します。「闷」は「こもる」と: Describes the humid, sticky heat from the rainy season into summer; 「闷」 means "stuffy, closed in." Dry heat is 「热」 and muggy heat is 「闷热」, and it's handy for everyday weather small talk.
今日は蒸し暑いね、エアコンつけよう。: It's so muggy today. Let's turn on the AC.
配信者の「応援してね」などに対し、「次は必ず」と返すネットのお約束。本当はやる気: An internet in-joke reply of "definitely next time" to streamers' requests like "please support me," jokingly implying you have no real intention. It's like "I'll try to make it" in English, used as a casual way of saying no.
今回の集まりは行けないや、次は必ず！: I can't make it to this get-together. Definitely next time!
買い物は何軒か比べてから決めなさい、という教え。大きな買い物の前によく使われ、ネ: The advice to compare several shops before deciding. It's often said before big purchases, and online too, as in 「先货比三家再下单」, expressing careful shopping habits.
スマホは焦って買わないで、いくつか比べてから決めよう。: Don't rush into buying a phone. Shop around before you decide.
仕事終わりや手伝ってもらった時に。ただし日本語ほど頻繁ではなく、本当に苦労した相: After work or when someone has helped you. It's not used as constantly as a casual "good job," though; it's natural as appreciation for someone who really did work hard, and a typical reply is 「不辛苦！」.
プロジェクトがついに完了しました。皆さんお疲れさまでした！: The project is finally finished. Thank you all for your hard work!
夏の定番のぼやき。「〜死了」で「死ぬほど〜」と強調します。中国の夏は地域によって: The classic summer grumble, with 「〜死了」 as the intensifier. Summers in China can approach 40°C in some areas, and southern cities such as Chongqing and Wuhan are famous for their heat and called 「火炉」 ("furnaces").
（心に）グッときた／刺さった: That hit me hard / That got me
ゲームの「防御が破られる」から。感動して涙腺が崩壊した時にも、図星を突かれて動揺: From gaming, "your defense has been broken." It's used both when you're so moved you start crying and when someone's remark hits a nerve, and you'll often see it in comments on touching videos.
母が書いてくれた手紙を見て、一気に涙腺崩壊した。: When I read the letter my mom wrote me, I just broke down.
相手と同じ気持ちや状況を伝える基本の一言。「我也很喜欢」「我也觉得」のように後ろ: The basic way to say you share someone's feelings or situation; you can also continue, as in 「我也很喜欢」 or 「我也觉得」. In the negative it becomes 「我也不〜」, so be careful not to say 「我也是不喜欢」.
あなたも辛いもの好きなの？私も！: You like spicy food too? Me too!
見慣れない料理や食材に出会った時に。中国の人は食べ方を喜んで教えてくれることが多: For when you come across an unfamiliar dish or ingredient. Chinese people are often happy to show you how to eat it, so it's a great conversation starter that makes eating on your travels more fun.
このカニ大きいね、これどうやって食べるの？: This crab is huge. How do you eat it?
学生が待ちに待った夏休みが始まった時の一言。中国の夏休みは7月中旬から8月末まで: What students say when the long-awaited summer vacation starts. In China it often runs from mid-July to the end of August, and a common joke is that kids' summer vacation is the parents' season of headaches.
やっと夏休みだ、お昼まで寝るぞ！: Summer vacation at last! I'm going to sleep till noon!
タクシーで行き先を伝えるとき。「师傅」は運転手や職人さんへの敬意ある呼びかけです: For telling a taxi driver where to go. 「师傅」 is a respectful way to address drivers and skilled workers, showing an address or map as you say it makes sure you get there, and ride-hailing apps are common too.
運転手さん、ここまでお願いします。だいたいどれくらいかかりますか？: Driver, please take me here. About how long will it take?

「大きな絵の餅を描く」が直訳で、実現しそうにない約束でやる気を出させること。上司: Literally "drawing a big pancake," motivating people with promises unlikely to come true. Employees often say it sarcastically when a boss verbally promises promotions or raises; it's like "pie in the sky" in English.
社長がまた空手形を切ってる、来年は必ず昇給だって。: The boss is making empty promises again, saying we'll definitely get a raise next year.
相手の意見に納得したときの相づち。「说得对（その通り）」より少し控えめな同意で、: A response when you're convinced by someone's view. It's slightly more reserved agreement than 「说得对」 ("that's right"), fine in meetings or casual talk, and 「很有道理」 strengthens it.
一理あるね、じゃあこのプランでやろう。: You've got a point. Let's go with this plan.
暑い日に冷たいものを提案する一言。「雪糕」は棒アイス、「冰淇淋」はソフトクリーム: Suggesting something cold on a hot day. 「雪糕」 is an ice pop or ice cream bar and 「冰淇淋」 is soft-serve or ice cream in a cup; 「根」 is the measure word for long thin things, so you say 「一根」 for an ice pop.
暑すぎる、コンビニでアイス食べよう！: It's too hot. Let's go to the convenience store and get a popsicle!
郷に入っては郷に従え: When in Rome, do as the Romans do
その土地に行ったら、その土地の習慣に従うこと。日本語のことわざとほぼ同じ意味です: When you go somewhere, follow local customs, the same idea as the English saying. You can use it in talk about travel or studying abroad: 「入乡随俗嘛！」.
中国では料理をみんなで取り分けて食べるんだ、郷に入っては郷に従えだね。: In China everyone shares the dishes at a meal. When in Rome, right?
鉄のように固い絆で結ばれた男友達のこと。「哥们儿」だけでも「仲間・相棒」の意味で: A male friend bonded as firmly as iron. 「哥们儿」 alone means "buddy, pal" and is often used by men to address each other, while a woman's best girlfriend is 「闺蜜」.
彼は大学時代からの大親友で、何でも話せるんだ。: He's been my best buddy since college. I can tell him anything.
ワンサイズ大きいのはありますか？: Do you have one size up?
服や靴の試着後に。小さいサイズなら「小一号」。中国のサイズ表記は日本と違うことが: After trying on clothes or shoes; for a size down, say 「小一号」. Chinese sizes may differ from what you're used to, so it's best to try things on.
この靴少しきついな、ワンサイズ大きいのありますか？: These shoes are a bit tight. Do you have them one size up?
夏に突然降る激しい雨のこと。「暴雨」は豪雨、通り雨なら「阵雨」。天気予報で「暴雨: A sudden heavy summer downpour: 「暴雨」 is a rainstorm, while a passing shower is 「阵雨」. When a 「暴雨预警」 (heavy rain warning) is issued, school and work plans may change, so check before heading out.
急に大雨だ、ちょっとお店で雨宿りしよう。: It's suddenly pouring. Let's wait it out in the shop for a bit.
メッセージやメールへの返事の定番。チャットでは「收到！」の一言で「受け取りました: The standard reply to messages and emails. In chat, 「收到！」 alone means "received, understood," and 「好的，收到」 is more polite.
了解です、午後に書類を送ります。: Got it. I'll send the documents over this afternoon.
気まずい、ばつが悪い時の一言。「尴尬」は日常でもネットでも頻繁に使われます。名前: For moments that are awkward or embarrassing; 「尴尬」 is used constantly in daily life and online, for example when you get someone's name wrong or a conversation falls silent. It covers both "awkward" and "embarrassing."
彼の名前を呼び間違えちゃって、気まずい…: I called him by the wrong name. So awkward...
食事代を自分が持つときの一言。中国では誘った側やおめでたいことがあった人がおごる: What you say when you'll pay for the meal. In China, the person who invited or who has something to celebrate often pays; the smart reply is 「下次我请」 ("next time's on me").
今日は私の誕生日だからごちそうするよ、好きなもの頼んで！: It's my birthday today, so it's on me. Order whatever you like!
冬は大根、夏は生姜を食べよ: Radishes in winter, ginger in summer
季節に合った食べ物で体を整えよう、という食養生のことわざ。冷たいものを取りすぎる: A food-as-medicine saying about balancing the body with seasonal foods. The idea is that in summer, when you have too many cold things, ginger warms you up, and it comes up often at Chinese family tables and in talk about health.
冬は大根、夏は生姜って言うし、夏でも冷たい水ばかり飲まないでね。: They say radishes in winter, ginger in summer, so don't keep drinking ice water just because it's summer.
英語のemotionalから。気分が落ち込んだり、センチメンタルになった時に軽く: From the English "emotional," used lightly when you feel down or sentimental. 「深夜emo」, suddenly feeling low late at night, is also a common phrase.
雨の日に家で一人、急にちょっとへこんできた。: Alone at home on a rainy day, I suddenly feel a bit down.
電車やバスで降りる駅を通り過ぎてしまった時の一言。「坐过了」とも言います。スマホ: For when you've gone past your stop on a train or bus, also 「坐过了」. It's an easy mistake when you're glued to your phone; follow up with 「下一站下车，再坐回去」 ("get off at the next stop and go back").
スマホ見てたら、乗り過ごしちゃった！: I was so busy looking at my phone that I missed my stop!
「谢谢」と言われたときの基本の返し。友達同士なら「没事儿」「小事儿（大したことな: The basic reply when someone says 「谢谢」; between friends 「没事儿」 or 「小事儿」 ("no big deal") are natural too. There's no need to be overly modest.
どういたしまして、これくらいお安いご用だよ！: You're welcome, it's nothing. No need to thank me!
夏の最も暑い「三伏天」が始まったことを表す言葉。7月中旬ごろから約1か月続きます: Says the hottest part of summer, 「三伏天」, has started; it begins around mid-July and lasts about a month. 今日から暑さ本番、これから1か月が一番暑いよ。: The dog days start today. The next month will be the hottest.
WeChat交換しよう: Let's add each other on WeChat.
中国で連絡先を交換するときの定番フレーズ。WeChatは連絡もSNSも支払いも一: The standard phrase for exchanging contacts in China. WeChat is essential infrastructure, handling messaging, social media and payments in one, and 「我扫你」 means you'll scan their QR code.
知り合えてうれしいです。WeChatを交換しましょう。: Great to meet you. Let's add each other on WeChat.
おいしいものに目がない人のこと。もともとは悪口でしたが、今は「我是个吃货」と自分: Someone who can't resist good food. It used to be an insult, but now it's established as a fun way to introduce your love of food, as in 「我是个吃货」, perfect for people who travel to eat.
私は食いしん坊だから、旅行は食べるのがメインなんだ。: I'm a foodie, so I travel mainly to eat.
急ぎすぎるとかえって目的を達成できないという意味。『論語』の言葉です。焦っている: Rushing too much keeps you from reaching your goal, a line from the Analects. It's perfect for advising someone who's in a hurry: 「别急，欲速则不达」.
急いで提出しないで、急がば回れだよ。もう一度確認しよう。: Don't rush to hand it in. More haste, less speed. Check it once more.
ネットで注文した荷物が届いた時の一言。中国では宅配便を「快递」と呼び、マンション: What you say when something you ordered online arrives. In China, deliveries are called 「快递」, and people often pick them up from parcel lockers in their building or pickup points; the excitement of waiting for a package is universal.
荷物届いた、ちょっと下まで取りに行ってくるね。: My package is here. I'll pop downstairs to get it.
がんばって！: Go for it! / You can do it!
試験、試合、仕事など、あらゆる場面で使える応援の定番。自分に言えば「がんばるぞ」: The go-to cheer for any situation: exams, games, work. Said to yourself it means "let's do this," and good replies are 「谢谢！」 or 「一起加油！」 ("let's both do our best!").
明日はもう試合だね、がんばって！みんな応援してるよ！: The game is tomorrow. Go for it! We're all behind you!
中国の夏の風物詩はスイカ。道端で大きなスイカを売る光景もよく見かけます。「得（d: Watermelon is the quintessential Chinese summer treat, and you'll often see big watermelons sold by the roadside. 「得（děi）」 means "have to," and cutting up a watermelon together as a family is a summer memory for many people.
こんな暑い日は、夏はやっぱりスイカでしょ！: On a day this hot, summer means watermelon!
すぐ対応します: I'll take care of it right away.
依頼やトラブルに素早く応えるときの一言。「马上」は「すぐに」。頼もしい印象を与え: A line for responding quickly to a request or problem; 「马上」 means "right away," and it makes you sound dependable. In chat, people sometimes just reply 「马上」.
おっしゃった件はすぐ対応します、少々お待ちください。: I'll deal with the issue you mentioned right away. Please wait a moment.
メッセージを「秒」で返すこと。返信がすごく速い人をほめたり、からかったりする時に: Replying to a message within "seconds," used to praise or tease someone who replies super fast. Reading a message but not replying is 「已读不回」, and a common joke is that you can't help replying instantly to someone you like.
彼にメッセージを送ると、いつも即レスしてくれる。: Every time I message him, he replies instantly.
仕事や旅行のあとにこぼす一言。「好」は「とても」の口語的な言い方です。言われたら: A complaint after work or a trip; 「好」 is a colloquial way to say "very." A kind reply is 「辛苦了，早点休息」 ("you've worked hard, get some rest").
一日中山登りして、あ〜疲れた。早く寝たい。: I hiked all day. I'm so tired, I want to go to bed early.

心を落ち着ければ暑さも感じにくくなる、という意味の言い回し。暑い暑いと騒ぐ人をな: A saying that if you calm your mind, you'll feel the heat less, often used to soothe someone complaining about the heat. It's close to the English advice "keep your cool."
暑い暑いって言わないで、心が静かなら涼しくなるよ。: Stop going on about the heat. A calm mind keeps you cool.
「打车」はタクシーを拾う・呼ぶこと。今は配車アプリで呼ぶのが主流で、それも「打车: 「打车」 means to catch or call a taxi. Nowadays most people call one with a ride-hailing app, which is also 「打车」, and 「打个车」 sounds more casual.
もう遅くて地下鉄が終わってる、タクシーで行こう。: It's too late, the subway's stopped. Let's take a taxi.
別れ際や手紙の最後で、相手の健康を気づかう言葉。特に遠くへ行く人や年配の人、忙し: Words of concern for someone's health when parting or at the end of a letter, especially for someone going far away, older people or busy people. It's also said 「多保重」, and it has a polite tone like "please take good care of yourself."
仕事は無理しすぎないで、くれぐれも体を大切にね。: Don't overwork yourself. Be sure to take care of your health.
真夏の外出や運動の前にかける気づかいの一言。「中暑」は熱中症・暑気あたり。中国で: A caring line before going out or exercising in midsummer; 「中暑」 means heatstroke or heat exhaustion. In China, mung bean soup, 「绿豆汤」, is the classic way to beat the heat and is often made at home.
昼の日差しは強烈だから、水をたくさん飲んで。熱中症に気をつけて。: The midday sun is brutal. Drink lots of water and watch out for heatstroke.
「性能と価格の比率」でコスパのこと。買い物レビューや口コミでよく使われます。逆は: Literally "the ratio of performance to price," it means value for money and is common in shopping reviews and word of mouth. The opposite is 「性价比不高」, and it's also handy to learn 「物美价廉」 ("good and cheap").
このイヤホン100元なのに音がすごくいい、コスパ最高だね。: These earphones are only 100 yuan and the sound is great. Excellent value for money.

今日は立秋だ、夜は焼肉で精をつけよう！: It's the Start of Autumn today. Let's go have barbecue tonight and fatten up for autumn!
もとはアルバイトの意味ですが、今は会社員が自分を指す自虐ネタとして定着。「打工人: Originally it meant a part-time worker, but now it's established as a self-mocking way for office workers to refer to themselves. The pep-talk line 「打工人，打工魂！」 ("worker by day, worker at heart!") also became a trend.
月曜朝の地下鉄は働く人でいっぱいだ。: The subway on Monday morning is packed with wage slaves.

しばらく会ってないね、会いたいな。いつ帰ってくるの？: We haven't seen each other in ages. I miss you. When are you coming back?
食事の終わりに。「ごちそうさま」にあたる決まり文句はないので、この一言や「太好吃: At the end of a meal. There's no set phrase for thanking for a meal, so this line or 「太好吃了」 conveys your thanks, and you can also use it to decline when offered more.
お腹いっぱいです、料理とってもおいしかった。ごちそうさまでした！: I'm full. The food was delicious, thank you for having me!
計画なしで思いつきで出発すること。特に「说走就走的旅行（思い立ったが吉日の旅）」: Setting off on a whim without a plan. The phrase 「说走就走的旅行」 ("a spur-of-the-moment trip") in particular expresses longing for carefree travel, like "spontaneous road trip" in English.
週末暇だし、思い立ったら即出発の旅をしよう！: I've got nothing on this weekend. Let's take a spur-of-the-moment trip!
三国志の曹操の話をしていたら本人が現れた、というたとえ。日本語の「噂をすれば影が: From the idea that you're talking about Cao Cao of the Three Kingdoms and the man himself appears. It's used exactly like "Speak of the devil" in English, the moment the person being talked about shows up.
噂をすれば影だね、ちょうどあなたの話をしてたところ！: Speak of the devil! We were just talking about you!
「鍋を放り投げる」が直訳で、責任や失敗を人に押しつけること。逆に人の責任をかぶる: Literally "to fling the wok," pushing responsibility or blame onto someone else; taking the blame for someone else is 「背锅」. It's a slightly sarcastic colloquialism used all the time in office chat and online.
プロジェクトに問題が出たら、彼はすぐ責任を押しつけ始めた。: As soon as the project ran into trouble, he started passing the buck.
夏の定番の誘い文句。中国では海南島や青島、厦門などの海辺の町が夏の人気旅行先です: The classic summer invitation. Seaside places like Hainan, Qingdao and Xiamen are popular summer destinations in China, and many people enjoy strolling on the beach and taking photos more than swimming.
休みになったし、一緒に海に遊びに行こう！: We're on vacation, let's go to the beach together!
置いていかれそうなとき、準備に時間がかかるときに。「等我一下」なら「ちょっと待っ: When you're about to be left behind or need time to get ready. 「等我一下」 means "wait a sec," and in chats 「等我五分钟」 ("give me five minutes") is standard.
待って！すぐ着替えるから。: Wait for me! I'll be changed in a second.
強いうらやましさを冗談っぽく表す一言。友達の旅行写真やおいしそうな料理の投稿への: A jokey way of expressing strong envy, a standard comment on friends' travel photos or posts of tasty food. Online, jealousy is likened to a 「柠檬」 (lemon), and people also say 「我酸了」 ("I've gone sour").
来月アイスランド行くの？うらやましすぎる！: You're going to Iceland next month? I'm so jealous!
わざと目立つ行動で周りを笑わせる人のこと。少しからかうニュアンスですが、愛嬌のあ: Someone who does attention-grabbing things on purpose to make people laugh. It's a bit teasing but also affectionate toward a charming person, and it can refer to the person who lightens the mood at work or school.
忘年会で踊るなんて、彼はほんと目立ちたがり屋だね。: He danced at the company year-end party. What a show-off.
中国の七夕（旧暦7月7日）は「中国のバレンタイン」と呼ばれ、恋人同士でプレゼント: China's Qixi (the 7th day of the 7th lunar month) is called "Chinese Valentine's Day," when couples exchange gifts. It has a different feel from the Tanabata festival as celebrated in Japan, where people write wishes on strips of paper.
七夕おめでとう！今夜は何食べたい？ごちそうするよ。: Happy Qixi! What do you want to eat tonight? My treat.
お腹がはち切れそうなほど食べた時の一言。「撑」は「張る」という意味です。「我吃饱: What you say when you've eaten so much you could burst; 「撑」 means "stretched, bloated." It's even fuller than 「我吃饱了」, and since Chinese dinners come with plenty of food, you'll have lots of chances to use it.
バイキングで食べすぎた、苦しい…: I ate too much at the buffet. I'm stuffed.
美術館や寺院、お店などで撮影の可否を確認する一言。フラッシュが禁止の場所も多いの: For checking whether photography is allowed in museums, temples, shops and so on. Flash is banned in many places, so 「能用闪光灯吗？」 is handy to know too; a no-photography sign reads 「禁止拍照」.
すみません、ここで写真を撮ってもいいですか？フラッシュは使いません。: Excuse me, can I take photos here? Without flash.
「挺」は「支える」という意味で、友達の決断や行動を全面的に支持する時に使います。: 「挺」 means "to support," used to fully back a friend's decision or action. You can strengthen it to 「无论如何我都挺你」 ("I've got your back no matter what"), and it's a standard comment online too.
会社辞めて起業したいの？応援するよ！: You want to quit and start your own business? I'm behind you!
仕事が終わった解放感を表す一言。チャットでは友達に「下班了，去吃饭吗？」と誘うこ: Expresses the relief of finishing work. In chats people invite friends with 「下班了，去吃饭吗？」; 「上班」 is going to work and 「下班」 is getting off work, and on days you get out on time you celebrate with 「今天准时下班」 ("left on time today").
やっと仕事終わった、今夜は火鍋行こう！: Finally off work. Let's have hotpot tonight!
予想が当たった時の一言。「ほらね」「思ったとおり」という感覚です。言い方によって: For when your prediction comes true, like "See?" or "Just as I thought." Depending on tone it can become a sarcastic "I told you so," and to praise someone you can say 「我就知道你能行！」.
やっぱり受かると思ってた、おめでとう！: I knew you'd get in. Congratulations!
夜食食べに行こう！: Let's go get a late-night snack!
夜遅くに友達を誘う一言。中国には屋台の串焼き「烧烤」やザリガニなど、夜遅くまで楽: A line for inviting friends out late at night. China has a late-night snack culture you can enjoy into the small hours, like street barbecue skewers, 「烧烤」, and crayfish, and eating outdoors on a summer night is special; it's also written 「宵夜」.
10時まで残業でお腹すいた、夜食食べに行こう！: I worked overtime until ten and I'm hungry. Let's go get a late-night snack!
短期間に多くの観光地を詰め込む、ハードな旅行スタイルのこと。軍隊の特殊部隊のよう: A grueling travel style that crams lots of sights into a short time, named after how tough military special forces training is. It spread as internet slang for the weekend trips of energetic young people.
2日で3つの町を回った、まさに弾丸旅行だよ。: We visited three cities in two days. Total special forces travel.
体ではなく心が疲れたことを表すネットでも日常でも使う口語。人間関係や面倒な手続き: A colloquialism, used online and in daily life, for being tired in the heart rather than the body. It's for when you're worn down by relationships or tedious paperwork, typically said with a sigh as 「好心累啊」.
彼にいくら説明してもわかってもらえない、もう疲れた。: I explained it to him for ages and he still doesn't get it. I'm so drained.
これは保証がつきますか？: Does this come with a warranty?
家電やスマホを買う時に保証の有無を確認する一言。「保修多久？（保証期間はどれくら: A line for checking the warranty when buying appliances or phones; learn 「保修多久？」 ("how long is the warranty?") with it. Note that without an official receipt, 「发票」, you may not be able to use the warranty.
この炊飯器、保証はつきますか？期間はどれくらい？: Does this rice cooker come with a warranty? For how long?
食べ物を勧められて断る時の定番の一言。「减肥」は体重を減らすこと。ただし中国では: The standard line for turning down food you're offered; 「减肥」 means losing weight. In China, though, saying 「我在减肥」 and then eating a late-night snack is a running joke, and you might hear 「明天再减」 ("diet starts tomorrow") in reply.
ありがとう、ケーキはやめておくね。ダイエット中なんだ。: Thanks, I'll pass on the cake. I'm on a diet.
了解の返事を重ねて、快く引き受ける気持ちを表します。チャットや電話でよく使う感じ: Repeating the "okay" shows you're happy to take something on, a pleasant reply common in chats and on the phone. Depending on the tone it can sound like an irritated "yeah, yeah," though, so say it brightly.
わかりました、明日の午前中にお電話します。: Okay, sure. I'll call you back tomorrow morning.

いざという時、遠くの親戚より近所の人のほうが頼りになる、という意味。日本語のこと: In a pinch, neighbors are more help than relatives far away. Use it when a neighbor has helped you or when talking about the importance of being on good terms with the neighbors.
お隣さんが1週間猫の世話をしてくれた、ほんと遠くの親戚より近くの他人だね。: My neighbor looked after my cat for a week. A near neighbor really is better than a distant relative.
立秋を過ぎても続く厳しい暑さを、虎にたとえた言葉。8月末から9月にかけて天気予報: A word likening the fierce heat that lingers after the Start of Autumn to a tiger, often heard in weather forecasts from late August into September. It's like "Indian summer" in English, used as in 「秋老虎来了」 or 「秋老虎还没走」.
立秋なのにまだこんなに暑い、残暑が厳しいね。: It's already past the Start of Autumn and still so hot. This lingering heat is brutal.
9月1日ごろの新学期の始まりに。中国の学校は9月が新年度で、日本の4月にあたりま: For the start of the new term around September 1; in China the school year starts in September. The classic picture is parents relieved, 「终于开学了」 ("school's finally started"), and kids sad the vacation is over.
新学期が始まった、また早起きの日々だ。: School's started again, so it's back to getting up early.
「振り返ったら会おう」で、近いうちにまた会う相手に軽く言うバイバイ。友達や同僚向: Literally "see you when I turn around," a light goodbye to someone you'll see again soon. It's a casual phrase for friends and coworkers, and 「明天见」 means "see you tomorrow."
先に会議行くね、またあとで！: I'm off to a meeting first. See you later!
「魚を手でつかむ」から転じて、仕事中にこっそり休むこと。職場の冗談として気軽に使: From "catching fish by hand," it means sneaking a break at work. It's used casually as an office joke, about as light as "just slacking off a bit" in English.
仕事中のサボりを社長に見られた、気まずい。: The boss caught me slacking off at work. So awkward.
理由がわかって納得した時の言葉。「怪不得他这么高兴（どうりで彼があんなにうれしそ: Said when you find out the reason and it all makes sense, as in 「怪不得他这么高兴」 ("no wonder he's so happy"). 「难怪」 means almost the same, and compared with 「原来如此」 it mixes surprise with understanding.
彼は北京出身なんだ、どうりで標準語がきれいなわけだ。: He's from Beijing? No wonder his Mandarin is so standard.

レストランで店員さんを呼んで注文するときに。「服务员」は呼びかけに使うのが普通で: For calling a server over to order in a restaurant; 「服务员」 is the normal way to address them. These days many restaurants also let you order on your phone by scanning a QR code.
すみません、注文お願いします！まず宮保鶏丁を一つ。: Excuse me, we'd like to order! First, one kung pao chicken.
商品の在庫がない状態のこと。ネットショップでは「暂时缺货（一時的に在庫切れ）」「: When an item has no stock left. In online shops you'll often see notices like 「暂时缺货」 (temporarily out of stock) and 「到货通知」 (restock alert), and when a popular item sells out people also say 「卖光了」.
この色は品切れで、来週入荷予定です。: This color is out of stock. It won't arrive until next week.
不幸に見えたことが幸運につながることもある、という教え。正式には「塞翁失马，焉知: The lesson that what looks like bad luck can lead to good fortune; the full form is 「塞翁失马，焉知非福」. Use it to cheer up a friend who's feeling down.
落ち込まないで、人間万事塞翁が馬、いいことかもしれないよ。: Don't be sad. It could be a blessing in disguise, maybe it's a good thing.
呼ばれた時やドアのチャイムが鳴った時の返事。重ねることで「すぐ行くよ」という慌た: A reply when someone calls you or the doorbell rings; doubling it gives a hurried "I'll be right there." Servers also say it when called to take an order, an everyday expression just like "Coming!" in English.
はーい、今行きます！ノックしなくても、すぐ開けるから。: Coming, coming! Stop knocking, I'm opening the door.
ホテルのフロントで。パスポートを出しながら言えば通じます。チェックアウトは「退房: At a hotel front desk; say it while handing over your passport and you'll be understood. Checking out is 「退房」, so 「我要退房」 does the job.
こんにちは、チェックインお願いします。ネットで部屋を予約しました。: Hello, I'd like to check in. I booked a room online.
9月10日は中国の教師の日。学生が先生に花やカードを贈ってお礼を伝えます。卒業し: September 10 is Teachers' Day in China, when students give teachers flowers and cards to say thank you. Many people still message their former teachers after graduating, and it's standard to add 「老师辛苦了！」.
王先生、教師の日おめでとうございます！ご指導ありがとうございます！: Happy Teachers' Day, Professor Wang! Thank you for your guidance!
謝られた時、心配された時、「どういたしまして」の代わりにも使える超便利フレーズ。: A super handy phrase for when someone apologizes or worries about you, and it can even replace "you're welcome." Adding 「儿」 is northern speech and gives it a friendly ring.
大丈夫、一人で帰れるから、送らなくていいよ。: It's fine, I can get back on my own. You don't need to see me off.
「干饭」はご飯をがっつり食べること。「干饭人，干饭魂」のように、食事を何より楽し: 「干饭」 means eating a hearty meal. Phrases like 「干饭人，干饭魂」 poke fun at yourself as someone who looks forward to meals above all, and inviting people at lunch break with 「走，干饭去！」 is classic.
12時だ、食いしん坊出動！: It's twelve o'clock. Foodies, prepare to move out!
電話応対、接客、会議など仕事のあらゆる場面で。「稍等一下」も同じ意味です。友達同: For every work situation: answering calls, serving customers, meetings. 「稍等一下」 means the same, and between friends 「等一下」 or 「等会儿」 is fine.
少々お待ちください、お調べします。: One moment, please. Let me check that for you.
久しぶりに会った友達に、変わっていないことを言う一言。見た目にも性格にも使えます: Said to a friend you haven't seen in a long time, about either looks or personality. It can be praise or teasing, so say it with a smile; the standard reply is 「你也一样！」.
10年ぶりだけど、相変わらずだね。全然変わってない。: Ten years and you're the same as ever, you haven't changed a bit.
買い物で一番使うフレーズ。指さしながら「这个多少钱？」と言えば完璧。答えの「块（: The phrase you'll use most when shopping; point and say 「这个多少钱？」 and you're set. 「块」 in the answer is the spoken form of 「元」 on price tags and means the same thing.
このリンゴは500グラムいくらですか？: How much are these apples per jin (500 g)?
相手の実力に感服した時にも、あきれて言葉が出ない時にも使える一言。「我服了你（あ: Used both when you're in awe of someone's ability and when you're too exasperated for words. 「我服了你」 ("you've got me beat") makes the admiration or exasperation toward the person clear, and the meaning depends on your delivery and tone.
彼一人でご飯5杯食べたよ、参った。: He ate five bowls of rice by himself. I give up.
もう少しゆっくり話してもらえますか？: Could you speak a bit more slowly?
聞き取れないときの救世主フレーズ。「我的中文不太好」を添えると相手もゆっくり話し: A lifesaver when you can't catch what's being said; adding 「我的中文不太好」 will get people to slow down. It may be the very first line a learner should memorize.
すみません、あまり聞き取れないので、もう少しゆっくり話してもらえますか？: Sorry, I don't quite understand. Could you speak a bit more slowly?
辛いものが苦手な人には必須の質問。ただ中国の人の「不太辣（あまり辛くない）」は日: An essential question if you can't handle spicy food. Note that when Chinese people say 「不太辣」 ("not very spicy") it can still be plenty hot for many visitors, so if you're worried, say clearly 「一点儿辣都不要」 ("no chili at all").
