フォローをお願いします: Could you follow up on this?
進行中の案件の確認や対応を同僚に頼む時の、職場の定番表現。「跟进」は「後を追って: A standard office expression for asking a coworker to check on or handle an ongoing matter. 「跟进」 means "to follow up and keep things moving," in the sense of tracking progress; if your boss says it to you, reply 「好的，我跟进」.
お客さんからまだ返事がないので、フォローをお願いします。: The client still hasn't replied. Could you follow up on it?
不安そうな相手を励ます一言。「有我呢（私がいるから）」を続けると頼もしい印象に。: A line to encourage someone who looks anxious; adding 「有我呢」 ("I'm here") makes you sound dependable. 「放心吧」 works in the same situations.
心配しないで、私がいるから大丈夫。: Don't worry, I'm here. It'll definitely be fine.
縁があれば遠くても巡り会う: Fate brings people together from afar
縁があれば千里離れていても出会える、という意味。遠い国の人と友達になった時や、偶: If fate wills it, you'll meet even a thousand li apart. Use it when you make friends with someone from a faraway country or to celebrate a chance meeting; it's like saying "it was meant to be."
東京と上海に住む二人が出会うなんて、まさに縁だね。: One of us in Tokyo and one in Shanghai, we were truly destined to meet.
花は美しく月は満ちる: blooming flowers and a full moon
花が美しく咲き、月が満月である様子から、家族の円満や幸せを願う言葉。中秋節や結婚: From beautiful flowers in bloom and a full moon, a phrase wishing a family harmony and happiness. It's often used in Mid-Autumn Festival and wedding messages, and as a four-character phrase it looks elegant written in a card.
中秋節、ご家族が円満で幸せでありますように！: Wishing your whole family happiness and togetherness this Mid-Autumn Festival!
旧暦8月15日、家族が集まり月を眺めて月餅を食べる大切な祝日。離れた家族を想う日: The 15th day of the 8th lunar month, an important holiday when families gather to admire the moon and eat mooncakes; it's also a day for thinking of family far away. Asking 「月饼你喜欢什么馅儿的？」 ("which mooncake filling do you like?") gets a conversation going.
中秋節おめでとう！今年はどんな餡の月餅を食べるの？: Happy Mid-Autumn Festival! What filling of mooncakes is your family having this year?
今夜の月、まんまるだね！: The moon is so round tonight!
中秋節の夜、家族や友達と月を眺めながら言う一言。中国では満月は「团圆（家族がそろ: Said while gazing at the moon with family or friends on Mid-Autumn night. In China the full moon symbolizes 「团圆」 (family reunion), and some people message family living far away that they're looking at the same moon.
早く出てきて見て、今夜の月まんまるだよ！: Come out and look, the moon is so round tonight!
「社交恐惧症」の略で、人付き合いが苦手なことを軽く言う表現。本来の医学用語より軽: Short for 「社交恐惧症」 (social anxiety disorder), a light way of saying you're not great with people. It's much lighter than the original medical term and used casually in self-introductions and small talk.
ちょっと人見知りで、初対面だとうまく話せないんです。: I'm a bit socially awkward, so I'm not good at chatting with people I've just met.
旅立つ人の無事を祈る見送りの言葉。飛行機に乗る人にはこちらが好まれることもありま: A send-off wishing a traveler a safe journey; some people prefer it for those flying. On arrival, it's good manners to send 「平安到达」 ("arrived safely"), and learn it together with 「一路顺风」.
道中気をつけてね、着いたらメッセージちょうだい！: Have a safe trip, and send me a message when you get there!
服なら試着、化粧品ならお試し、食べ物なら試食にも使える便利な表現。「试」は「試す: A handy phrase for trying on clothes, testing cosmetics or sampling food. 「试」 means "to try," and it combines into words like 「试吃」 and 「试穿」.
このシャツ、試着してもいいですか？: Can I try on this shirt?
散財させちゃってすみません: You shouldn't have spent so much.
おごってもらった時や、プレゼントをもらった時にかける恐縮の言葉。「破费」はお金を: A line of appreciation and embarrassment when someone treats you or gives you a gift; 「破费」 means making someone spend money. It's like "Oh, you shouldn't have!" in English, and the other person replies 「哪里，应该的」.
こんなに高いプレゼント、気を遣わせちゃってごめんね。: Such an expensive gift, you really shouldn't have.
良いことの実現には多くの困難がつきもの、という意味。日本語の「好事魔多し」に近い: It means good things usually come with many obstacles along the way. In Chinese it's used as encouragement, "good things come after hardship," a bit like "the course of true love never did run smooth."
ついに結婚するんだね、いろいろあったけどおめでとう！: You two are finally getting married. Good things really do take time!
10月1日の建国記念日「国庆节」のあいさつ。ここから約1週間の大型連休「黄金周」: A greeting for 「国庆节」, the National Day on October 1. It kicks off the roughly week-long holiday 「黄金周」 (Golden Week), when travel and trips home fill the whole country; for people enjoying the holiday, adding 「假期愉快！」 is natural.
国慶節おめでとう！皆さん、よい連休を！: Happy National Day! Enjoy the holiday, everyone!
誕生日の定番のお祝い。チャットで送ることも多く、紅包（お祝い金）を添える人も。返: The standard birthday greeting. It's often sent by chat, and some people include a red envelope of gift money; replying 「谢谢！」 with a smiley emoji is perfect.
誕生日おめでとう！これプレゼント、開けてみて。: Happy birthday! Here's your present, open it!
人が山や海のようにいっぱいいる様子。連休の観光地や人気イベントの混雑を表すのにぴ: Crowds of people like mountains and seas. It's perfect for describing crowds at tourist spots during holidays or at popular events, a four-character idiom used all the time in everyday conversation.
国慶節の万里の長城は人だらけで、全然進めない。: The Great Wall during National Day was a sea of people. You could barely move.
高速が駐車場状態だ: The highway's turned into a parking lot.
連休中の大渋滞を冗談まじりに言う表現。中国では祝日に高速道路が無料になることがあ: A jokey way to describe heavy holiday traffic jams. In China, highways are sometimes toll-free on public holidays, so car travel all happens at once; 「堵车」 means a traffic jam, and it's the same scene as holiday-weekend gridlock anywhere.
国慶節の初日、高速は駐車場状態だよ。: First day of the National Day holiday, and the highway's a parking lot.
「对不起」「不好意思」と謝られたときの返し。相手を安心させるやわらかい言い方です: The reply when someone apologizes with 「对不起」 or 「不好意思」, a soft way to put them at ease. More casually, 「没事儿」 is common.
気にしないで、私たちも今来たところだから。さあ座って！: It's okay, we just got here too. Have a seat!
「我的青春回来了」の略で、子どものころ好きだったアニメや歌、お菓子が復活した時に: Short for 「我的青春回来了」 ("my youth is back"), internet slang for when cartoons, songs or snacks you loved as a kid make a comeback. 「爷」 ("grandpa," i.e. "yours truly") is a playful way to say "I," and it's a standard comment on nostalgic things.
子どもの頃見てたアニメの新作が出た、青春が戻ってきた！: A new version of the cartoon I watched as a kid is out. My childhood is back!
「加班」は残業のこと。同僚とのぼやきに使えます。言われたら「辛苦了！」でねぎらい: 「加班」 means working overtime, good for grumbling with coworkers; if someone says it to you, show appreciation with 「辛苦了！」. Working on a weekend is also called 「加班」.
今日も残業だ、晩ご飯はデリバリーだな。: Overtime again today. Dinner will have to be delivery.
長い連休のあと、仕事や学校のリズムに戻れずだるくなる状態のこと。国慶節や春節の後: Feeling sluggish after a long holiday because you can't get back into the rhythm of work or school. It's often talked about after National Day or Spring Festival, like "post-vacation blues" in English, and used half-jokingly.
連休が終わって、今日は休みボケで全然だめだ。: The holiday's over, and today at work the post-holiday blues hit hard.
グラスを合わせるときの掛け声。本来は「杯を空にする」の意味で、宴席では一気飲みを: The toast when clinking glasses. It originally means "dry the cup," and at banquets you may be pressed to drink it all in one go; if you can't, saying 「随意」 ("as you like") is fine.
赤ちゃんや動物、かわいい小物を見た時の一言。「可爱」は日本語の「かわいい」とほぼ: Said when you see a baby, an animal or a cute little thing. 「可爱」 means "cute" but is rarely used for adult men, and online people sometimes double it as 「可可爱爱」.
お宅のワンちゃんかわいすぎる、なでてもいい？: Your puppy is so cute! Can I pet it?
相手の都合を気づかう、やわらかい依頼の表現。「方便」は「都合がいい」。急ぎでない: A soft request that's considerate of the other person's schedule; 「方便」 means "convenient." It's handy for saying something isn't urgent, and it leaves a much better impression.
急ぎじゃないので、お手すきの時に返信してもらえれば。: No rush, just reply whenever it's convenient.
秋の空が高く澄み、空気がすがすがしい様子を表す四字表現。秋の天気をほめたり、遠足: A four-character phrase for the high, clear autumn sky and refreshing air, perfect for praising autumn weather or inviting people on an outing or hike. Autumn is said to be Beijing's most pleasant season.
秋晴れで爽やか、まさに山登りにぴったりの季節だね。: The autumn air is crisp and clear, just the right time for hiking.
「調子どう？」「中国語どう？」と聞かれて、謙遜まじりに答える定番。「马马虎虎」は: The standard modest answer when asked "How are you?" or "How's your Chinese?" 「马马虎虎」 also originally means "careless, sloppy," so using it about someone else's work is a criticism.
私の中国語はまあまあかな、まだ勉強中なんだ。: My Chinese is so-so. I'm still working hard on it.
ネットショッピングで複数人が一緒に注文し、割引や送料無料の条件を満たすこと。友達: Several people ordering together online to meet the conditions for a discount or free shipping; you ask friends or coworkers 「一起拼单吗？」. 「拼」 is also used for sharing deliveries or taxi rides.
200元以上で送料無料だから、一緒に注文しよう！: Free shipping over 200 yuan, so let's order together!
秋は上海ガニ「大闸蟹」の旬。メスは旧暦9月、オスは10月がおいしいと言われ、カニ: Autumn is the season for the hairy crab, 「大闸蟹」; females are said to be best in the 9th lunar month and males in the 10th, and talk of crab signals autumn's arrival. It's also often used as an excuse to invite friends out for a meal.
秋だね、カニがおいしい季節。週末カニ食べに行こう！: Autumn's here, and so is crab season. Let's go eat crab this weekend!
相手の意見を聞くとき、判断をゆだねるときの一言。「你觉得呢？」も同じ。少し強く言: For asking someone's opinion or leaving the decision to them; 「你觉得呢？」 means the same. Said a bit forcefully, it becomes a rhetorical "isn't it obvious?"
この件どうしたらいいと思う？あなたはどう？: What should we do about this? What do you think?
旧暦9月9日の重陽節は、高齢者を敬う「敬老节」でもあります。祖父母や年配の家族に: The Double Ninth Festival on the 9th day of the 9th lunar month is also 「敬老节」, a day to honor the elderly. People call grandparents and older relatives or climb a mountain together with them, and adding 「身体健康」 to messages for older people is appreciated.
おじいちゃん、重陽節おめでとう！健康でいてね！: Grandpa, happy Double Ninth Festival! Wishing you good health!
失敗は成功のもと: Failure is the mother of success
失敗が成功の土台になる、という励まし。日本語と同じ発想です。試験や仕事でうまくい: Encouragement that failure lays the foundation for success, the same idea as the English saying. It's a positive thing to say to a friend whose exam or work didn't go well.
今回うまくいかなくても大丈夫、失敗は成功のもとだよ。: It's okay that this exam didn't go well. Failure is the mother of success.
相手の反応や心配が大げさだと感じた時に使う一言。「そんなに〜するほどのことじゃな: For when you feel someone's reaction or worry is exaggerated; it means "it's not worth going that far." You can be specific, as in 「不至于这么生气吧」 ("no need to get that angry").
5分遅れただけでそこまで怒らなくても、機嫌直して。: I was only five minutes late. No need to get so angry, come on.
領収書をもらえますか？: Can I get an official receipt?
出張や経費精算で必要なときに。中国の「发票」は税務上の正式な領収書です。会社名と: For when you need one for a business trip or expense claim; a Chinese 「发票」 is an official receipt for tax purposes. You may be asked for your company name and tax ID, so having them ready makes it smooth.
すみません、領収書をもらえますか？会社で精算するので。: Hi, could I get an official receipt? I need to claim it from my company.
カフェやホテル、友達の家で使える一言。中国語ではWi-Fiを「无线网」と言うほか: Useful in cafés, hotels and friends' homes. In Chinese, Wi-Fi is called 「无线网」 or simply "WiFi," and many places print the password on the receipt or post it on the wall.
すみません、ここのWi-Fiのパスワードは何ですか？: Excuse me, what's the Wi-Fi password here?
秋は雨のたびに寒くなる: Each autumn rain brings more cold
秋は雨が降るたびに気温が下がっていく、という季節のことわざ。天気の雑談や、家族に: A seasonal saying that every autumn rain brings the temperature down another notch, used in weather small talk or when telling family to dress warmly. It captures exactly the feeling of autumn getting colder with each rainfall.
秋は一雨ごとに寒くなるから、明日は上着を一枚多めにね。: Each autumn rain brings more cold, so remember to wear an extra jacket tomorrow.
「团队建设」の略で、会社の同僚と一緒に食事や旅行、スポーツをするイベントのこと。: Short for 「团队建设」, a company event where coworkers eat, travel or play sports together. It's meant to bring people closer, but when it's held on a day off some people grumble, "team building again?"; think company trips and social gatherings.
今週の土曜は会社のチームイベントで、郊外でバーベキューだよ。: The company has a team-building event this Saturday, a barbecue in the countryside.
強く後悔している気持ちを大げさに表す一言。「早知道就不〜了（こうなるとわかってい: An exaggerated way of expressing strong regret, typically followed by 「早知道就不〜了」 ("if I'd known, I wouldn't have ..."). It's common in casual situations, from shopping mistakes to oversleeping.
昨日セールのコートを買わなかったの、今めちゃくちゃ後悔してる！: I didn't buy that discounted coat yesterday, and now I regret it so much!
「突進する」の意味から、何かに挑戦する時やセールに飛び込む時の掛け声に。ネットで: From "to charge forward," it's a rallying cry when taking on a challenge or diving into a sale. Online, doubling it up as 「冲冲冲！」 for momentum is standard, and you can cheer a friend on with 「冲啊！」 too.
コンサートのチケットは10時から販売開始、行くぞ！: Concert tickets go on sale at ten. Let's go!
品質が良くて値段が安い: good quality at a low price
品物が良く、しかも安いことを表す四字表現。お店の宣伝文句や口コミでよく見かけます: A four-character phrase for goods that are good and cheap at the same time, often seen in shop slogans and reviews. It's similar to 「性价比高」 but a bit more literary, and it can also praise a market or an eatery.
この小さな店の商品は良くて安いから、学生に大人気だよ。: This little shop's stuff is good and cheap, so students love coming here.
急に冷え込んだ日に家族や友達を気づかう一言。「降温」は気温が下がること、「保暖」: A caring line for family and friends on a day that suddenly turns cold. 「降温」 means the temperature dropping and 「保暖」 means keeping your body warm, and the phrase is common in weather app notifications too.
明日は急に冷え込むから、出かける時は暖かくしてね。: There's a big temperature drop tomorrow, so keep warm when you go out.
家で仕事をすること。「远程办公（リモートワーク）」とも言います。「今天在家办公」: Doing your job at home, also called 「远程办公」 (remote work). You might tell coworkers 「今天在家办公」, or the company may order it on days with bad weather; it's the same as "WFH" in English.
今日は大雨だから、会社から在宅勤務の指示が出た。: It's pouring today, so the company told everyone to work from home.
人々にとって食べることが何より大切だ、という意味の古い言葉。食いしん坊が冗談で「: An old saying that eating matters more than anything to people. Foodies also use it jokingly as an excuse, "food comes first, right?", and it shows the passion of Chinese food culture.
食べることが一番大事、まずご飯を食べてから仕事の話をしよう。: Food comes first. Let's eat, then talk about work.
困った時に真の友情がわかる: A friend in need is a friend indeed
苦しい時こそ本当の気持ちや友情がわかる、という意味。日本語の「まさかの時の友こそ: Hard times show people's true feelings and friendships, close to "A friend in need is a friend indeed" in English. Using it to thank a friend who helped you really gets your feelings across.
入院中毎日お見舞いに来てくれたね。困った時に本当の友達がわかるよ。: You came to see me every day when I was in the hospital. A friend in need is a friend indeed.
会話を切り上げる時の気軽な一言。電話やチャットの最後によく使います。「回头再聊」: A casual line for wrapping up a conversation, often at the end of a call or chat; 「回头再聊」 means the same. It's handy when you're truly busy, but if you're cutting someone off, adding 「不好意思」 is more polite.
もう車に乗るから、また今度話そう！バイバイ！: I'm getting in the car now. Talk to you later! Bye!
何度も聞くより一度見るほうがよくわかる、という意味。漢字も意味も日本語とほぼ同じ: Seeing something once tells you more than hearing about it a hundred times, like "seeing is believing" or "a picture is worth a thousand words." Try saying 「真是百闻不如一见！」 when you're traveling.
ここの景色はまさに百聞は一見に如かず、写真よりきれいだ。: The scenery here really proves seeing is believing. It's even more beautiful than in the photos.
そろそろ股引の季節だね: Time to put on long johns.
「秋裤」は防寒用の長いインナーパンツ。寒くなると中国の親が子どもに「穿秋裤！」と: 「秋裤」 are long underpants worn for warmth. Chinese parents telling their kids 「穿秋裤！」 as it gets cold is such a cliché it's an internet joke, and the word symbolizes family concern as the seasons change.
どんどん寒くなってきた、そろそろ股引はかなきゃ。: It's getting colder and colder. Time to put on long johns.
季節の変わり目に家族や友達を気づかう一言。中国の親が子どもによく言うセリフでもあ: A caring line for family and friends as the seasons change, and a line Chinese parents often say to their kids. When someone says it to you, reply 「知道了，你也是！」.
寒くなったから暖かくしてね、風邪ひかないように。: It's getting cold, so bundle up and don't catch a cold.
疲れている人や夜遅くまで働く人への気づかいの一言。チャットの締めくくりにもよく使: A caring line for someone who's tired or working late, often used to close a chat. 「早点睡」 means the same and is more colloquial; a natural reply is 「好，你也是，晚安」.
今日はお疲れさま、早く休んでね。: You worked hard today. Get some rest early.
中国の食卓で何度も聞く、もてなしの言葉。料理を取り分けてくれることも多いです。お: A hospitable phrase you'll hear again and again at Chinese tables, and people will often serve food onto your plate. If you're full, reply with a smile: 「够了够了，谢谢」.
たくさん食べて、これ全部あなたのために作ったんだから！: Eat more, I made all these dishes especially for you!
開き直って投げ出す: to give up and let it all go
どうせうまくいかないなら、とわざと努力をやめてしまうこと。もとはスポーツの用語で: Deliberately ceasing to try because things won't work out anyway. It originally comes from sports, and online it's used self-mockingly, as in 「今天摆烂了」 ("zero motivation today").
宿題が多すぎる、今日はもう開き直って何もしない。: There's too much homework. I'm just giving up for today.
行き先までの距離を確認したいときに。「走路要多久？（歩いてどれくらい？）」と続け: For checking the distance to where you're going; it helps to follow up with 「走路要多久？」 ("how long on foot?"). Even if they say 「不远」, it can turn out to be surprisingly far...
すみません、博物館はここから遠いですか？歩いてどれくらいですか？: Excuse me, is the museum far from here? How long does it take on foot?
運が悪いことが続いた時のぼやき。「倒霉」は不運なこと。「今天真倒霉」「倒霉透了（: A grumble when bad luck keeps coming; 「倒霉」 means bad luck. It's used as in 「今天真倒霉」 or 「倒霉透了」 ("the worst"), much like "Just my luck!" or "What a day!" in English, and you'll hear it often.
傘を忘れたらまた雨に降られた、ついてない！: I forgot my umbrella and got caught in the rain again. Just my luck!
割引条件に届くよう買い足す: to add items to hit a discount threshold
「〇元以上で〇元引き」の「满减」の条件を満たすため、ほかの商品を足すこと。セール: Adding other items to meet the conditions of a 「满减」 deal, "X yuan off when you spend Y." It's a classic headache during sales, and friends sometimes club together with 「一起凑满减」.
割引条件に届かせるために、お菓子をもう一袋足した。: To hit the discount threshold, I added another bag of snacks.
カートの中身を全部買う: to empty the shopping cart (buy it all)
ネットショップのカートに入れておいた商品を一気に買うこと。セール時期の目標として: Buying everything you've saved in an online shopping cart in one go. People declare it as a sale-season goal, as in 「今年双十一要清空购物车！」, and it often goes together with the self-mocking 「剁手」 (overspending).
1か月待って、今夜ついにカートの中身を全部買える。: After waiting a month, tonight I can finally empty my shopping cart.
双十一で何買った？: What did you buy on Double 11?
11月11日の大型ネットセール「双十一」の時期に交わす定番の会話。もとは独身者の: A standard conversation around 「双十一」, the giant online sale on November 11. It started as Singles' Day, 「光棍节」, but is now the biggest shopping event of the year; common answers are like 「买了一堆日用品」.
双十一で何買った？私は新しい炊飯器を買ったよ。: What did you buy on Double 11? I bought a new rice cooker.
「手を切り落とす」というネット発の自虐表現。衝動買いや爆買いを反省しつつ笑う時に: A self-mocking internet expression meaning "chop off my hands." It's used when laughing at your own impulse buys or shopping sprees while regretting them, often during sales like 「双十一」.
双十一でまた買いすぎた、来月は節約生活だ。: I overspent again on Double 11. Next month I'll be eating dirt.
安心して！任せて！: Don't worry! Leave it to me!
「心を下ろして」が直訳。頼まれごとを引き受ける時や、相手を安心させたい時に。日本: Literally "put your heart down." Use it when taking on a request or reassuring someone; it has a dependable ring, close to "Leave it to me" in English.
この件は私に任せて、安心して！: Leave this to me, don't worry!
会議中です、後ほど折り返します: I'm in a meeting, I'll call back later.
電話に出られない時に送るメッセージの定番。「稍后」は「少し後で」。スマホの自動返: The standard message to send when you can't take a call; 「稍后」 means "a little later," and it's also used in phones' auto-replies. In formal situations, 「我在开会，稍后给您回电话」 with 「您」 is more polite.
すみません、会議中なので後ほど折り返します。: Sorry, I'm in a meeting. I'll call you back later.
北方では11月中旬ごろから、地域全体で集中暖房「暖气」が始まります。暖房が入ると: In the north, district-wide central heating, 「暖气」, starts around mid-November. Once it's on, it's warm enough indoors for short sleeves, and it's a seasonal topic people have been eagerly waiting for; the south basically doesn't have it.
やっと暖房が入った、部屋がずいぶん暖かくなった！: The heating's finally on. The room is so much warmer!
「永远的神（永遠の神）」のピンイン頭文字。一時期大流行した言葉で、今はやや古い印: The pinyin initials of 「永远的神」 ("forever a god"). It was hugely popular for a while and now feels a bit dated; knowing it helps you read online posts, but don't overuse it.
この店の牛肉煮込み麺はまさに神！: This place's braised beef noodles are the GOAT!
どうして来たの？（うれしい驚き）: What are you doing here? (pleasant surprise)
思いがけず人が来た時の驚きの一言。言い方によっては「何しに来たの？」と迷惑そうに: A line of surprise when someone turns up unexpectedly. Depending on tone it can sound like an annoyed "what are you here for?", so say it with a smile; it's often used where English would say "Oh, you came!"
えっ、どうしたの？今日は残業って言ってなかった？: What are you doing here? Didn't you say you had to work late today?
値段交渉の第一声。市場や観光地の露店で使えますが、デパートやチェーン店では値引き: The opening line in haggling. It works at markets and stalls at tourist sites, but department stores and chains normally don't give discounts, and the trick to negotiating is to say it with a smile.
Tシャツ1枚300元？高すぎる！: 300 yuan for a T-shirt? That's too expensive!
今あるもので満足できる人はいつも幸せだ、という意味。欲張らずに今を楽しむ生き方を: People who are satisfied with what they have are always happy, a philosophy of enjoying the present without being greedy. It's close to "contentment is true wealth," and older people often say it.
仕事は安定してるし、家族も元気。足るを知るだね。: My job is stable and my family is healthy. Contentment brings happiness, right?
即答できないときに使える大人のフレーズ。「我确认一下再回复您（確認してからお返事: A grown-up phrase for when you can't answer on the spot. Saying 「我确认一下再回复您」 ("I'll check and get back to you") sounds polite and reassuring, even in business.
この日程を確認して、改めてお返事します。: Let me check this date and get back to you.
寒い日に火鍋を食べに誘う一言。「该」は「〜すべき、〜でなくちゃ」。中国の火鍋は地: A line for inviting someone out for hotpot on a cold day; 「该」 means "should, has to." Chinese hotpot comes in many regional varieties, from fiery Sichuan to Beijing's mutton hotpot, and a 「鸳鸯锅」 is a split pot with spicy and non-spicy broths.
外こんなに寒いし、冬はやっぱり火鍋でしょ！: It's so cold outside. Winter means hotpot!
軽いおわび、人に声をかける時、恐縮する時に幅広く使えます。「对不起」より軽く、日: Used widely for light apologies, getting someone's attention or feeling embarrassed. It's lighter than 「对不起」, a very handy word that covers both "excuse me" and "sorry."
すみません、ちょっと通してください。: Excuse me, could I get past?
代弁者: someone who says what you're thinking
自分が言いたかったことを代わりに言ってくれる人のこと。「你就是我的嘴替（あなたは: A person who says what you wanted to say for you, as in 「你就是我的嘴替」 ("you said exactly what I wanted to say"). It's often seen in replies to comments people relate to.
このコメント、まさに言いたかったこと全部言ってくれた！: This comment is so right. It says exactly what I was thinking!
いってらっしゃい！道中お気をつけて: Bon voyage! Have a good trip!
旅に出る人を見送るときの定番。「順風に乗って」というイメージ。ただし飛行機に乗る: The standard send-off for someone setting out, with the image of "a favorable wind." Some people, however, feel 「一路平安」 is better for someone taking a flight.
道中お気をつけて、向こうでも体に気をつけてね！: Have a good trip, and take care of yourself over there!
驚いたり、信じられないことが起きたりした時の感嘆詞。「我的天哪！」と強めることも: An exclamation for when you're shocked or something unbelievable happens, often strengthened to 「我的天哪！」. It works for good and bad things alike, like "Oh my God!" or "No way!" in English.
なんてこった！鍵を部屋に閉じ込めちゃった！: Oh my God! I locked my keys in the room!
食事が終わって支払いたいときに。手を挙げてこう言えばOK。「结账」も同じ意味です: For when you've finished eating and want to pay; just raise your hand and say this. 「结账」 means the same, and you'll often see friends "fighting" over who pays.
すみません、お会計お願いします！QRコードで払えますか？: Excuse me, check, please! Can I pay by QR code?
ブランド品や化粧品を買う時に、偽物でないかを確認する一言。「正品」は正規品のこと: A line for making sure brand goods or cosmetics aren't fakes; 「正品」 means genuine goods. Online shops often display 「保证正品」 (authenticity guaranteed), and at markets it's fine to ask straight out.
このバッグこんなに安いけど、本物ですか？: This bag is so cheap. Is it genuine?
一日千秋の思い: One day apart feels like three years
一日会わないだけで三年も離れたように感じる、という意味。恋人や親しい人への想いを: Not seeing someone for just one day feels like being apart for three years, expressing longing for a partner or someone close. It's also fun to say jokingly to a friend you haven't seen in a while.
離れてたった一日でもう会いたい、一日千秋の思いだよ。: We've only been apart a day and I miss you already. One day apart feels like three years.
電話に出る時の基本のあいさつ。「喂」は電話の呼びかけで、2声で「wéi」と発音す: The basic greeting when answering the phone. 「喂」 is the phone "hello" and is often pronounced in the second tone, 「wéi」; in business, you identify yourself with 「喂，您好，这里是〜」 ("Hello, this is ...").
驚く話を聞いた時の定番リアクション。「本当なの、嘘なの？」が直訳。友達同士のくだ: The standard reaction to surprising news, literally "is it true or false?" It's casual and for friends, so with superiors 「真的吗？」 ("really?") is safer.
来月結婚するの？マジで？: You're getting married next month? For real?
ご飯の約束をする: to make plans to eat together
友達と食事の約束をすること、または食事に誘うこと。「约个饭吧」「周末约饭吗？」の: Making a date to eat with friends, or inviting someone to eat, as in 「约个饭吧」 or 「周末约饭吗？」. It's a casual expression used a lot in young people's chats, like "let's grab food" in English.
しばらく会ってないね、今週末ご飯行かない？: We haven't seen each other for ages. Want to grab a meal this weekend?
必要以上に努力を競い合って、皆が疲弊する状態。勉強や仕事でよく使われます。「别卷: A state where everyone competes harder than necessary until they're all worn out, often used about school and work. People also say 「别卷了」 ("stop competing so hard") jokingly.
みんな塾に通ってて、競争が激しすぎる。: Everyone's signing up for cram classes. The competition is insane.
1時間も並んだ: I waited in line for an hour.
人気店やアトラクションで長く並んだ時の一言。中国の人気店は「排队」が当たり前で、: A line for when you've queued a long time at a popular restaurant or attraction. Queuing, 「排队」, is a given at popular places in China, and some use apps to get a place in line; pair it with 「值了」 ("worth it") afterwards.
この店1時間も並んだけど、本当においしかった。並んだ甲斐があった！: I waited in line an hour for this place, but it was really delicious. Totally worth it!
初対面の名刺交換で。両手で渡すのは中国でも礼儀正しいとされます。ただ最近はWeC: For exchanging business cards at a first meeting. Handing it over with both hands is considered polite in China too, but these days people often exchange WeChat contacts and skip the cards.
はじめまして、こちらが私の名刺です。よろしくお願いします。: Hello, here's my business card. I look forward to working with you.
心を打たれた時の素直な一言。映画や本、友達の気遣いなどに。日本語の「感動」と同じ: An honest reaction when something moves you, such as a movie, a book or a friend's thoughtfulness. 「感动」 is used much more casually than "deeply moved" in English, and people say 「好感动」 even for small kindnesses.
私の誕生日覚えててくれたんだ、感動！: You remembered my birthday? I'm so touched!
慣れれば自然と上達するという意味。語学学習にぴったりの言葉です。「多练习，熟能生: Getting used to something naturally makes you better at it, perfect for language learning. Saying 「多练习，熟能生巧！」 makes for encouragement like "Keep at it, practice makes perfect!"
漢字を書くのは最初は難しいけど、慣れればうまくなるよ。たくさん書けば大丈夫。: Writing Chinese characters is hard at first, but practice makes perfect. Just write a lot.
乗ったら寝て、降りたら写真: Sleep on the bus, snap photos off the bus
団体ツアー旅行を皮肉るおなじみの言い回し。移動中は寝て、観光地では写真を撮るだけ: A familiar line poking fun at group tours: you sleep while traveling and just take photos at the sights, so you remember nothing. It's perfect for getting a laugh when sharing travel stories.
ツアー旅行って、乗ったら寝て降りたら写真撮るだけだよね。: Group tours are all about sleeping on the bus and taking photos off the bus.
試験、面接、試合など大事な場面の前に。英語のGood luck!にあたります。「: Before important moments like exams, interviews or games, the equivalent of the English "Good luck!" Combining it with 「加油」 as 「加油，祝你好运！」 really gets your feelings across.
明日面接だよね？幸運を祈るよ！: Your interview's tomorrow, right? Good luck!
濡れ衣を着せられる: to take the blame (for someone else)
「鍋を背負う」が直訳で、他人の失敗の責任をかぶること。責任を押しつける「甩锅」の: Literally "to carry the wok on your back," taking the blame for someone else's mistake, the opposite of 「甩锅」 (passing the buck). It's used when grumbling at work, as in 「我又背锅了」 ("I got blamed again").
明らかに私のミスじゃないのに、結局私のせいにされた。: It clearly wasn't my fault, but in the end I took the blame.
朝のあいさつ。職場では「早！」と一文字だけで済ませることも多く、それがむしろ自然: The morning greeting. At work people often just say 「早！」, which actually sounds more natural, and you can reply 「早！」 too; the evening 「晚上好」 sounds a bit formal.
家に帰った時のあいさつ。中国語には「ただいま」「おかえり」の決まり文句がなく、こ: The greeting when you get home. Chinese has no fixed pair of phrases for "I'm home" and "welcome back," so this line is often used, and the natural response is 「回来啦！」; some families don't say it every time.
お母さん、ただいま！今日の晩ご飯なに？: Mom, I'm home! What's for dinner tonight?
野次馬見物: to watch the drama (as a bystander)
話題の出来事を傍観して楽しむこと。「吃瓜群众（野次馬たち）」もよく使います。ゴシ: Watching a hot topic from the sidelines and enjoying it, literally "eating melon"; 「吃瓜群众」 (the melon-eating crowd) is common too. It's a self-mocking way to describe yourself watching gossip or a scandal unfold.
この件は私には関係ないから、横で見物してるだけ。: This has nothing to do with me. I'm just watching from the sidelines with my popcorn.
料理が足りない時や、もう少し食べたい時の提案。中国の外食では大皿料理をみんなで分: A suggestion when there isn't enough food or you want a bit more. Eating out in China usually means sharing big plates, so ordering more to match the number of people is normal, and it's often used when treating guests.
人が多くて料理が足りないね、もう一品頼もう。: There are a lot of us and not enough food. Let's order another dish.
私、大変すぎる…: Life is so hard for me.
困難が重なった時に冗談めかしてこぼす流行語由来の表現。深刻ではなく、ちょっと笑い: From a viral catchphrase, a joking complaint when troubles pile up. It's not serious, more a grumble with a laugh in it, and suits chats between friends.
仕事は山積み、子どもまで熱を出して、もう大変すぎる。: Work is piling up and now my kid is sick too. Life is so hard.
ネットショップで返品後、お金が戻ってきたことを伝える一言。「到账」は口座に入金さ: Saying the money has come back after returning something to an online shop; 「到账」 means arriving in your account. People also often ask 「钱到账了吗？」 to confirm a transfer, an expression typical of China, where mobile payment dominates.
服を返品したら、もう返金が入ってた。: I returned the clothes, and the refund has already come through.
一年の仕事の成果をまとめる年末恒例の報告書や会議のこと。会社員にとって12月の悩: The annual end-of-year report or meeting summing up a year's work results, a December headache for office workers. These days personal posts looking back on the year are also called 「年终总结」, often seen on social media.
また年末だ、まだ年末の振り返りを書き始めてない。: It's the end of the year again, and I haven't even started my year-end review.
遠慮しないで！: Don't be shy! / Make yourself at home!
友達がお礼を言いすぎたり遠慮したりするときに。中国では親しい間で礼を言いすぎると: For when a friend is thanking you too much or holding back. In China, too much thanking between close friends can feel distant; you can also say 「咱俩谁跟谁啊」 ("come on, it's us").
遠慮しないで、好きなもの取って。自分の家だと思ってね！: Don't be shy, help yourself to whatever you want. Make yourself at home!
ご飯のおとも動画: a show to watch while eating
食事中に見る動画やドラマのこと。ご飯のおかずの漬物「榨菜」のように、食事に欠かせ: Videos or dramas you watch while eating. Internet slang meaning it's as essential to a meal as 「榨菜」, the pickled mustard greens eaten with rice; 「下饭剧」 means almost the same and is often discussed as a way to enjoy eating alone.
このバラエティは私のご飯のおとも、食事のたびに見てる。: This variety show is my mealtime viewing. I watch it every time I eat.
迷った末に決めたときの一言。「了」で「決めた！」という気持ちが出ます。レストラン: A line for when you've finally decided; 「了」 adds a feeling of "decided!" It's also handy when settling on your order in a restaurant.
どっちも好きだけど、よし、これにします！: I like both of these, but... okay, I'll take this one!
大学院入試がんばって！: Good luck on your grad school exams!
12月下旬に行われる大学院の全国統一入試「考研」の受験生への応援の言葉。毎年多く: Encouragement for candidates taking 「考研」, the national graduate school entrance exam held in late December. It's an important exam many young people take every year, so it's a perfect pep talk for those studying in libraries toward year-end.
試験まであと1週間、院試がんばって、きっと合格できるよ！: One more week until the exam. Good luck on your grad school exam, I'm sure you'll make it!
冬至に餃子食べた？: Did you eat dumplings for the winter solstice?
北方では冬至に餃子を食べる習慣があり、「食べないと耳が凍える」という言い伝えも。: In the north people eat dumplings on the winter solstice, and there's a saying that if you don't, your ears will freeze. In many parts of the south people eat 「汤圆」 (sweet rice balls) instead, which makes the regional differences a fun topic.
今日は冬至だよ、餃子食べた？: It's the winter solstice today. Did you eat dumplings?
後になって知ったことを悔やむ一言。「早知道〜就〜了（〜と知っていたら〜したのに）: A line for regretting something you found out too late, often in the pattern 「早知道〜就〜了」 ("if I'd known ..., I would have ..."). It's an everyday expression, close to "If only I'd known!" or "You should've told me!" in English.
今日こんなに寒いってわかってればなあ、薄着すぎた。: If only I'd known it would be this cold today. I'm way underdressed.
旅先での一大事に使う一言。まず警察で「报案（届け出）」をして証明をもらい、大使館: For a serious emergency while traveling. First go to the police to file a report, 「报案」, and get a certificate, then go through the procedures at your embassy or consulate; 「丢了」 means "lost" and works for wallets and phones too.
すみません、パスポートをなくしてしまいました。どうすればいいですか？: Officer, I've lost my passport. What should I do?
12月24日のクリスマスイブのあいさつ。中国ではイブに「平安果（リンゴ）」を贈る: A greeting for Christmas Eve, December 24. In China there's a custom of giving a 「平安果」 (an apple) on Christmas Eve, because 「平」 and 「苹」 are pronounced the same, and beautifully wrapped apples line shop shelves.
よいクリスマスイブを！リンゴをどうぞ、無事に過ごせますように！: Merry Christmas Eve! Here's an apple for you, stay safe and well!
中国でも都市部ではクリスマスがイベントとして人気。イブにはリンゴを贈る習慣があり: In Chinese cities, too, Christmas is popular as an event. There's a custom of giving apples on Christmas Eve, apparently because 「平安夜」 (Christmas Eve) and 「苹果」 sound alike.
メリークリスマス！今夜一緒にクリスマスツリー見に行こう！: Merry Christmas! Let's go see the Christmas tree together tonight!
すみません、地下鉄の駅はどう行けばいいですか？: Excuse me, how do I get to the subway station?
道をたずねる基本形。「请问」をつけると丁寧です。「〜怎么走」の前に行き先を入れ替: The basic form for asking directions; adding 「请问」 makes it polite. Swap in any destination before 「〜怎么走」 and you can ask your way anywhere, and using a map app alongside is reassuring.
すみません、地下鉄の駅はどう行けばいいですか？まっすぐですか？: Excuse me, how do I get to the subway station? Do I go straight ahead?
あなたがいてくれてよかった: I'm so glad I have you.
助けてくれた人や、いつもそばにいてくれる人への感謝の言葉。友達にも家族にも恋人に: Words of gratitude for someone who has helped you or is always there for you, fine for friends, family or a partner. It's a little embarrassing to say, but it's a warm expression perfect for thanking someone for the year at year's end.
この一年ずっとそばにいてくれてありがとう。あなたがいてくれてよかった。: Thank you for being by my side all year. I'm so glad I have you.
笑えば十歳若返る: Smile and you'll look ten years younger
笑うと若返る、だからいつも笑顔でいよう、という俗語。日本語の「笑う門には福来る」: A folk saying that smiling makes you younger, so keep smiling. It's a positive saying, close to "laughter is the best medicine," and saying it jokingly to someone who's down or frowning lightens the mood.
そんな浮かない顔しないで、笑えば若返るよ！: Don't look so glum. Smile, and you'll look ten years younger!
古い年を送り新しい年を迎える: to see out the old and ring in the new
年末年始のあいさつや挨拶状に使う四字表現。会社の忘年会のスピーチやカードにぴった: A four-character phrase for year-end and New Year greetings and cards, perfect for a speech at a company year-end party or a card. It's a bit literary, but you'll often hear it on TV New Year's Eve shows.
一年を締めくくり新年を迎えるにあたり、皆さんよいお年を！: As we see out the old year and ring in the new, Happy New Year, everyone!
一緒に年越ししよう！: Let's ring in the New Year together!
大晦日の夜を一緒に過ごし、カウントダウンをしようと誘う一言。「跨年」は年をまたぐ: An invitation to spend New Year's Eve together and do the countdown; 「跨年」 means crossing into the new year. Young people often go out to events and countdowns with friends, and 「跨年夜」 is New Year's Eve.
今年最後の日、一緒に年越ししよう！: It's the last day of the year. Let's ring in the New Year together!
大晦日に別れる時の冗談まじりのあいさつ。実際は翌日にまた会うのに「来年会おう」と: A jokey goodbye when parting on New Year's Eve; the fun is saying "see you next year" when you'll actually meet the next day. You can use it in place of "Happy New Year" as a parting greeting. Here's to the new year!
今年の話はここまで、また来年！: That's enough chatting for this year. See you next year!
